 ¥S am particularly happy to go through the manuscript
of Shri Subrata Kumar Banerjea's Synoptic Memorizer of
Materia Medica. The reason for this is that | have not
come across someone himself a student of the College
who has put in such diligence and produced a worth-while
book. Having himself gone through the mill recen
  known the difficulties of his colleagues, he has particularly
 written it for their benefit as its name suggests. However,
 1 feel that even those in the profession would considerably
 profit from its study. So far, he has;covered only fifty
 remedies and | do hope that he will bring out further
 volumes to cover the rest of the Materia Medica.
 A mere glance at the different headings and the
 chapters gives an insight into his vast study and great
 labour in writting this book.
 There fas often been a debate as to whether the
Materia Medica should give the personality profiles or the
key-notes. From the name of the bodék. one may be
inclined to put it in the latter category. However, looking
through it, one finds a blend of both as some explanation
or details of the outstanding symptoms are mentioned
with many of the remedies.
 The Repertorial references and the Comparative Materia
Medica, so essential for an accurate prescribing, are very
welcome aspects of this book.
 There are many Materia Medicas that are available
and the question can be asked is there need for more? My
answer is that every author looks at the gem of our
remedies from a different angle and sheds a new lIustre by
bringing ‘out some fresh points or at least arranging it in
a new form.
 As mentioned above, it would be particularly welcomed
by the students of the homoeopathic institutions especially
when they are preparing for their examinations.

 Co write a new Materia Medica is a greatest
absurdity,—it can only be delineated in a new approach
and illustration, to reiterate in a novel fashion, to cope with
the needs. Thus with this book also,—it is a synopsis of
different views and styles of presentation of drug-pictures
as adopted by our immortal Master Samuel Hahnemann,
our delightful Kent, iamented Hering, erudite Dunham,
sagacious Clarke, discreetful Nash- prudent Allen etc. etc.
| have liberally taken references from their classic literatures,
with a view to generate enthusiasm and to arouse the latent
curiosity of the young homoeopathiec generations in those
treasure references,—the store-house of knowledge, as
they are really our precious wealth. For this reason ! have
mentioned their good-names, whenever their views has
been expressed.
 Throughout the book, reader may note that repeatedly
{ have obliged to mention, ‘Master Kent’—adoptation of
this style has néver intended to demote the honour of that
prodigious personality, the versatile genius, our imperishable
Master Samuel Hahnemann, but only to impress the readers
and above all to generate interest and curiosity in Kent’s
literatures; as it is perhaps only ‘Master Kent’ who can
delineate and depict the drug-picture in our mind in a
lucid comprehensible fashion; besides this he is regarded
as ‘Master’ by many renowned authorities throughout the
globe for his masterly dedication of many classic literatures
to the homoeopathic fraternity.
 The appearance of this book has never intended to
Jeplace the text-books or our wealthy literatures, but only
 to imprint the drug-pictures in the faculty of intutiqn in a
more comprehensible fashion. Hence | have adopted my
own technique to enumerate every drug-picture and mental-picture in such a comprehensible fashion so that they can
be memorized easily such as, know the medicine through
the name of the medicine or through any suitable denotative
connotation, viz. Sulphur through the word Philosopher,
Thuja through the tips Sycosis, Bryonia through the tips
Modality etc. etc. This expedient of memorizing our vast
Materia Medica is entirely designed by me and thus I am
presenting this artistic style before the homoeopathic
fraternity. | think this fashion of memorizing our vast Materia
Medica will serve some beneficial purpose, espcially for the
examinees, as well as those. are in the profession.

 The heart-felt desire of many of my coaching students,
and above all my dearest parents’, my Bara-Ma’s and many
of my friends inspiration has set my heart on taking this
venture.
 The major part of this book was originally my personal
notes, but for this purpose they have been thoroughly
designed and profusely augmented. The mental pictures
and the drug-pictures are some-what voluminous, at least
from the examination point of view : but my actual intention
is to depict the picture in a broad and elaborated fashion,
elucidating different views from different angles, for quick
and vivid comprehension ;—to make the gist. will not be of
problem, provided they grasp the thought.

 On coming to an end, | must commemorate the sacred
memory of my past homoeopathic generations—my
homoeopathic ancestors, those have descended me the ‘true
haemoeopathic blood’—perhaps the rooct-cause of my
deepest regard ia this ‘divine art of healing’.
 { must acknowledge with honour the names of my
revered professors,—Dr. P. C. Paul, Dr. S. K. Dubey,
Dr. Sripati Mandal, Dr. T. P. Mandal, Dr. S. R. Saha,
Dr. M. M. Dutta, Dr. Mahendra Singh, Dr. Gopal Mukherjee,
Dr. N. K. Mitra, Dr. S. C. Ghosh, Dr. D. Tarafdar, Dr. H. P.
Saha. Dr. K. N. Chakraverty. Dr. J. Barman, Dr. B. Santra,
 and Dr. Ashit Banerjee, those have encountered their best
possible endeavour in teaching me this ‘rational art’, and my
all success is due t0 them and to be conferred upon them
as their success ; my gratitlide to them.
 | must convey my sincere regards and gratitude to my
dearest parents, as they are my constant source of inspira-tion and my beloved ‘Bara-Ma’, whom | endearingly revere
and her dedication is ineffable. Their immense love was the
only key to my success.
 Last but not the least, {am obliged to mention the
names of Kajal Bhattacharyya, Satyajeet Sinha, Debabrata
Sarkar, Akhilesh Khan, Swapan Paria, Samir Pyne and
Madhumeeta Mitra, as their constant inspiration, un-stining
help and co-operation, un-ending patience in every regard
has made this effort possible, yet | can not narrow down
our relation by mere thanking them, as such a relation
does not exists amongst us,—our relation is above such
courtesy.
 Lastly, | am frankly inviting afl sorts of constructive
suggestions and this is to confess that if this book can
win the heart of the readers, thence that will be my finest
yeward.

 Subrata Kumar Banerjea.

Note .1.:
 | have angmented the Materia Medica through
Repertorial references, thus reader will note the style viz.
Acon.? which explicits that Aconite covers that symptom
in first grade; viz. Acon ® ie in second grade; Acon.* ie
in third or lowest grade. Though in correct sense, Acon.*
means Aconite getting threa marks, i.e. covering the
symptom in first grade but it may create mis-conception for
the beginers. Thus here Acon.* means first or highest grade,
which will leave away the possibilities of any mis-concep-tion for the beginers.
Note .2 :
 All the quotations reader may not find in the specific
chapter, viz. ‘Chill begins in lumbar region, Natrum Mur. ;

chapter. ( Ref. Nash. ).
 Not a single symptom or symptom-complex has been
quoted emperically, but reader may find those in targer
reference literatures, viz. Dr. Clarke’s Dictionary of Materia
Medica. Dr. Allen’s Encyclopaedia of Pure Materia Medica,
Dr. Hering’s Guiding Symptoms etc. etc.

 causations.

 Mental ailments resulting from bad effects of :
 i) Fear, fright (Gels., Hyos., Opium.).
 if) Vexation. (Bry., Chamo.) (Ref. Dr. Talcott.).
 iii) Shock.
 iv) Excitement.
 v) Grievances (Staph.) (Ref. Tyler).
ll. Onset :
 Characterized by intensity and acuteness. It was our
lamented Dr. Dunham who has compared the onset of
Aconite with a violent storm.
il, Character:
 i) Anxiety :
 The anxiety of Aconite pt. is due to the internal.
turmail and hence the pt. is*restless. This anxiousness of
the mind is evidenced by her fnteffectuat tension which is
 2 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

reflected as great acuteness of all her senses. Her senses of
smell, sight, touch etc. becomes exceedingly Ayperactive.
 in the mental sphere this hyperactivity is specially
evidenced as she gets vexed at tritles.
 in the physical sphere it is evidenced as slight bearable
pain to her becomes unbearable she jumps in agony, a
State of hyperaesthesia. Dr. Hering said due to this mental
anxiety he is agonized and tossing about.
 Note : Fear of future and forebodings also charac-terizes this anxiety
li) Calmness contraindicates Aconite :
 Dr. Guernsey said, “Mental ca/mness contraindicates
Aconite. (Chamo.— indicates, Puls ).
 Thus whenever Aconite will be the drug of choice,
there must be the mentaf uneasiness, mental restlessness,
worry, anx/ety and great fear, otherwise it is contraindicated

 iil) Overwhelming fear :
 It is one of our leading remedy having different charac-teristic types of fear.
 it has) got not that type of fear viz., fear of poverty
like. Bryonia. fear of thunder like Phos.; fear of dogs like Bell.;
fear of approach like Arnica. fear of being alone like Ars,
Arg Nit.; but it has got that characteristic fear, that is fear of
death with prediction of day and time of death.
 Dr. Tyler said, fear of death may be so _ great, that
people have actually killed themseives for fear of dying.
 Hence Aconite.* has got fear of death (Ars.!, Calc. Carb.?,
 Cimicifuga’, Gels.*, Lac Can.1, Nit. Ac.*, Phos.?, Platina‘) (Ref.
Kent's Repertory) but the characteristic is pt. predicts the day;
even the time of death, i. e., the clairvoyance. Master Kent
sald, many times the pt actually predicts the moment or
hour of death: if a clock is in the pt.‘s room, she may say,
that when the hour hand reaches a certain point, she will be
a corpse. Dr. Tyler said. i is Aconite pt. who calls her
friends around her and takes leave of them. Foar
 of death

chapters.content:
is such an important feature. Dr. Farrington said that
prediction of hour of the death esp. in childbed is also found
in it and can be bracketed with Argentum Nit. and Coffea.
 Besides this :
(a) fear of darkness ( Can. Ind.*, Strarmo.?, Acon.?, Calc. C.?,
 Camph.?, Carb. An.?, Carb. Veg.*, Caust.?, Cup.?, Lyco 2,
 Phos.?, Puls.?. )
{b) fear of bed ( Acon.*, Ars.*, Caust.*, Cup.*, Lach.” }
(c) fear of ghost ( Acon.*, Ars.?, C.V.*, Caust.?, Lyco.*,
 Phos.?, Puls.%, Sulph.? )
{d) fear of going out, fear of crawd ( Acon.”, Arg. N.?,
 Lyco.?, Nat. Mur *, Nux Vom 2, Puls.® ).
Note : Dr. Nash said, ‘fear to go into society’"—
 Anthrapophabia.
{e) fear of death in pregnancy (Acon.*).
(f) fear of approaching death (Arg. Nit., Ars , Cimic., Nit. Ac.,
 Secale Cor.) (Ref. Cowperthwaite).
(g) fears the loss of reason—leading to mental prostration with
 weakness of memory, can not remember dates. (Ref.
 Dr Talcatt’s Mental diseases).

iv) Nash’s trio of restless :
 Aconite is one of the Nash's trio of restless medicines.
Aconite is mentally restless, where as Rhus Tox. is physically
restless and Arsenic is restless both mentally and physically
thus the trio ; Acon., Ars. Alb., and Rhus Tox.
 Dr, E. B. Nash said, fear, as much as the pain that makes‘
the pt. so full of that agonized restlessness.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury said, the impatience and anxiety
makes the pt. restiess. She throws herself about and cons-tantly changes the position. The true reason of this restless-ness is to be found in a state of internal turmoil and anxiety
and agony. She moans and laments, screams and shouts,
not knowing what to do and how to find consolation.
 In such a case of mental restlessness, Aconite will be
the drug of cholse ;—give her drug— it will] cure.
  4 Synoptic Memerizer of Materia Medica

 v) iIgnatia like hysterical :
 Aconite patient is also inclined to be hysterical. (Caust.!,
 Gels.*, Ign.?, Lach.2, Nat Mur.*, Nit. Ac.7, Nux Vom.*, Puis.?,
 Sep.*, Sil.4) Dr N. M. Chowdhury said, great variation of
 Mood and temperament. She is cheerful this minute, weeps
 the next. She is sad and taciturn now but gay and
 foquacious the next moment.
 Master Kent said, sometimes Acontte pt. looses all her
 affection, which leads to a state of indifference—this state
 is also characterized by Aysterical mood.
 Dr. Talcott said pt. moves from dry anyuish to exuberant
 tears.
 vi) Tension is the key-note :
 Dr. Huge said, tension is the key note of Aconite pt.
 ( —Congestion is the keynote of Belli. ).
 This tension is mentally evidence by intense restlessness,
 inconsolable anxiety, acute imagination and fears.
vii) Uncommon peculiar sensations :
 It has got some peculiar sensations. viz.,
 a) All the intellectual functions are going on in the
region of the stomach.
 b) Some parts of the body is deformed e.g., a limb is
displaced, fips are too thick. ( Ref. Farrington ).
viii) Music makes her sad :
 Music is unbearable for Aconite pt.; it makes her sad
( Acon.?, Graph.*, Dig.*, Kreos.*, Nat.C.*, Thuja.?,)
( —music > Aurum.”, Tarent.? ).
Note. 1 :
Countenance :
 Master Kent has pointed to note the countenance of
Aconite, which is expressive of fear. Fear is depicted upon
her countenance.
Note. 2:
 Dr. Kent reported that every mental condition ig marked
by intensity. If it is a delirium, thence it is intense ; ——thus
  MENTAL PICTURES 5

Dr. Farrington said the intensity of these symptoms denotes
overexcitement of brain, common enough to hysterical
patients.
Note. 3:
 Master Kent said, this type of mental picture is always
present in pneumonia, inflammatory conditions of any part,
or kidney, liver, bowels etc.
Note. 4 :
 In case of females amenorrhoea in plethoric young girls
after fright is a marked feature.
Note. 5 :
 Our immortal Master Hahnemann said ‘whenever Aconite
is chosen homoasopathically, you must above all, observe
the moral symptoms, and be careful that it cioselfy resembles
them ; the anguish of mind and body: the restlessness; the
disquiet not to be allayed’
Note. 6:
 Master Kent said even congestion of parts as a result of
fear. A turmoil affecting the whole sensorium.
iv) Modality :
 Mental symptoms < in the evening, towards night.
Q. Mental picture of ANTIM CRUD.
 Remember it through the name of the medicine.
 A = Angry child.
 N = No desire to live.
 T = Timidity.
 ] = Irresistable desire to talk in rhymes.
 M = Moonlight <.

 C = Commits suicide by drowning.
 R = Repeat verses.
 U = Unsatisfied.
 D = Dull.
ft. Mental Causations :
 a) Bad effects of disappointment of love ( Hyos.*,
 Ign.2, Nat. Mur.*, Phos.Ac.*, Aur.?, Cal.P?, Hell.*, Lach.?,
 6 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

Staph.*, Caust.?, Nux. Vom.*). ( —love sick, Ant.C.*; —love
with sifent grief, [gn.*, Nat. Mur.*, Phos Ac.*).
1. Character :
 i) Angry child :
 Ant. Crud. is a medicines suits for extremes of life ( Verat.
Alb. }—affecting child and aged. Hence Ant. Crud. child bears
a pecullar mentality.
 it can be compared with the race of swine for the virtue
of the fact that it inclines to grow Zet and mecreover its typical
obstinacy.
 The chifdis angry and obstinate, fretful, peevish, can’t
bear to be touched or to be looked at, sulky, does not wish
to speak or be Spoken to ( Ant Tart.; lod.; Sil.). Angry
at every little attention.
 Becomes angry at silly matters, il-humour characterizes the
angry chiid.
Note. 1: Dr. Farrington said this peevish mental state is
 associated with nausea, hot and red face and irregular
pulse.
Note. 2: Dr. Farrington said the child is particularly cross
 when washed in cold water.
iit) No desire to live :
 itis tiger prescriber Tyler Kent who has elucidated the
picture.
 Master Kent said, it produces a very serious state of mind,
an absence of the desire to live. Pt. says, ‘Oh. doctor, if i
could only die’—such an aversion, loathing of life is confined
to Ant. Crud. pt.
Note. 1: Master Kent said this state is especially found in a
low, lingering, continued fever such as typhoid. Such a
typhoid will sometimes be seen in young giris about puberty,
who are threatening to go into chlorosis. They have loathing
of life, but it is a Aysterical loathing of life
Note. 2: Dr. Henry Clarke said disgust of life, with an incli-nation to blow one’s brain out, to drown oneself. Great
anxiety about his fate and inclination to shoot himself.
  MENTAL PICTURES 7

iii) Timidity :
 Timidity is another feature. The pt is timid, morose
and there is graat sadness berne in the mind
 Dr. Farrington said pt. is sulky and sad like Puls.
iv) trresistable desire to talk in rhymes :
 There is an /srresistable desira to talk in poem whichis
common enough to hysterical women.
v) Moonlight <. :
 Over-sxcitable, nervous, hysterical, ecstatic young girls and
women are overcome by moeilow-light from the moon—and
there is ‘sentimental mood especially in the moonlight’
( Ref. Kent ).
 Master Kent said, it ts a hysterical state, a disorderly
outburst of the affections, which especially aggravated in
the moon-light.
Note. 1 :
 Dr N. M. Chowdhury said Ant C. is moon-struck.
Note. 2 :
 Dr Farrington said in some cases there is a erotic condition
of mind, connected with sexual erethism.
vi) Commit suicide by drowning :
 Ant Crud pt wants to commit suicide by drowning
( Bell ?, Hell.*, Hyos.*, Lach?®, Puls °, Rhus Tox.*) ( —by
hanging, Ars.?,—with knife, Ars?, Calc C*, Merc? ; —by
shooting, Ant. C.?
vii) Repeat verses :
 This is a marked peculiarity that Ant. Crud opt. like to talk
in verses. Pt. also repeat verses esp in the moonlight.
vili) Unsatisfied :
 Dr. John Henry Clarke satd pt. is not satisfied though
whatever is done for him This ts a peculiar mentality borne
in Ant. C. pt.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury also said that the baby whines and
cries and nothing pleases him.
 Dr. Talcott reported in his book ‘Mental diseases’ —that has
amorous longings, not for any living creature, but for some
unseen seraph boded forth by an ecstatic imagination
  S Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 ix) Dull :
 Dr. Clarke reported that Ant. Crud pt. is dull. Dutiness of
 intellect, imbecility.
 Hil. Modality :
 < in open fire (Kent said, open fire is wholly against the
 Ant Crud. pt.) ; < in moon-light.
 Note. : Dr. Talcott said it is suited to the mental condition of
 some young persons passing through the critical pubescent
 period, whose growing interest in the opposite sex tends to
 center unhealthfully.

 Q. Elucidate the mental picture of ARGENTUM NITRICUM.
 1 like to impress you the entire mental picture through the
word—-ARGENTUM.
 A= Apprehension, anxious.
 R=Reserved, sad.
 G=Great haste.
 E= Excitable, easily angered.
 N= Notions, Nervous, Neglected.
 T=Tendency to suicide.
 U= Undue fear of projecting buildings.
 M= Memory loss.
1. Mental Causations :
 1) Apprehension.
 ii) Fear.
 iii) Mental stress and strain.
 iv) Acute or chronic diseases from unusual or jong-continued mental exertion.
 v) Symptoms comes on as a result of his anxiety (Kent).
 vi) Dr. Talcott said mental symptoms results from over-indulging in the use of alcohol and excess in venery.
Il. Character :
 a) Apprehension and anxiety : There is a great
 apprehension which Master Kent in his voluminous Repertory
kept in the subrubric: anxiety, anticipating an engagement
(Arg. N.*, Gels.*, Medo.?).
 Anxiety and apprehension when getting ready to go to
ch urch, opers, examination, or any other engagement and at
  MENTAL PICTURES 9

that diarrhoea sets in 1. e., apprehensive d/arrhoea (Gels.).
 Dr. Tyler said, it is one of the great remedy of examination
funk (Aethusa., Gel., Kali Phos., Anac.)
 Dr. Tyler said, pt. breaks into sweat with anxiety when
‘going to a wedding, to church, to opera.
 b) Reserved : _.
 Our Arg. Nit. pt. is reserved, introvert in their disposition.
Pt. is sad taciturn, gloomy.
 Dr. Farrington said in some cases we find profoud
melancholy.
 c) Great haste :
 The pt. is very much /mpulsive, does everything in a great
haste, even eats and drinks in a great haste, must walk fast.
 Dr. Farrington said pt. seems to be always busy yet
accomplishes nothing. He hurries restlessly to fulfill an
engagement, thinking that he will be too late, hence does
everything in a great haste.
 In Dr. Kents’ Repertory it has been placed to the sub-rubric
—hurry to arrive for the appointed time. (Arg Nit.*) -—hurry
while walking (Arg Nit.*, Sulph Ac.*, Tarent.*, Sulph.?,
Thuja.?),—hence time passes too slowly ( Can Ind.*, Glon.*,
Alumina.?, Arg. N.2, Medo.?, Merc.2, Nux Mos.*, Nux Vom.? )
— too quickly, (‘ Cocc.*, Therid.*),
 da) Excitable :
 Arg Nit. pt. are easily excitable, easily angered — which
brings on pain in head and chest.
 6) Notions :
 Strange notions crowded in Arg Nit. pt.
 Master Kent said, dread of crowd.
 Pt. has a strange notion that some serious incurable
disease has overtaken him, imagines that if he left afone, he
will die. Dr. Farrington said apprehension of some incurable
diseases of brain.
 Builds casties in air in the day and sees monstrous visions
at night.
 10 Synoptic Memorizer of..Mlateria Medica

 Dr. Talcott in his Book ‘Mental disease reported that Arg
Nit. pt. hesitates to undertake anything from the fear of
failure ( Arnica. ).
 Arg. Nit. also possesa strange notion that he has been
neglected and despised by everybody and thus finds no
pleasure in his Iife.
 Dr. Tyler said that Arg Nit. has also c/austrophobia —\ e.,
fear of confinement, which is a strange notion [t has also
got anthropophobia { Acon.’, Arg N* Aur.*, Nat. Mur.?
N.V ®, Puls.?}) and dreads certain places.
 f) Tendency to suicide :
 Suicidal tendency prevails upon the pt. when crossing
through high altitudes, bridge etc. On looking down from
high altitude creates a peculiar type of /mpulses to jump out
of the place Master Kent tn his Repertory classed it in the
sub-rubric—throwing himself from a height (Aur.?, Arg N.?,
Vell.*, N.V.?).
 Master Kent reported fear of death, often predicts the
moment of death.
 g) Undue fear of projecting buildings :
 Arg Nit. pt. has great fear of projecting buildings and
corners which creates a sensation as if it would fall over him
 The sight of the projecting buildings makes the pt. d/zzy
 Dr. Farrington has remarked about this fear of projecting
buildings and corners that it is due to the m/stake of esti-mation of distances ie., derangement of the sense, derange-ment of the sense of distance, depth and magnitude — altitude
sense derangement, so that the pt. thinks that he will run
against those and have a clash.
 Dr Tyler said even in the street the s/ght of high houses
always made him giddy and caused him to stagger. It seem
as if the houses on both sides would approach and crush him.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury reported that this altitude sense
derangement is due to imperfect co-ordination of occular
muscles.
 h) Memory Loss :
 There is frequent loss of memory, makes frequent fault in
  MENTAL PICTURES 1t

speech, because he can not find right word during conver-sation.
 Master Kent said, disturbance in the memory. Irrational
in his explanations of his actions and methods.
QO. Enumerate the mental picture of AURUM METALLICUM.
 | like to depict the mental picture of Aurum Metallicum
through the name of the remedy.
 A=Anxlous abuut future.
 U=Unpardonable crime and sins.
 R=Realisation of them.
 U=Unwanted element.
 M-- Melancholia

 M = Miserable life.

 U=sUnhappy.
 M== Mental causations—Marcurial bad effect etc.
1. Mental causations :
 i) Grief.
 ii ) Disappointed love
 iii) Reserved displeasure, unfulfilled fongings ( Ref. N. M.
 Chowdhury ).
 iv) Vexation, mortification.
 v) Fear, fright.
 vi) Contradiction.
 vii) Mercurial and syphilitic bad-effect.
 Note : Syphilitic miasm engrafted on scrofulous base.
 ll. Character :
 i) Anxious about future :
 Our typical Aurum. pt. is anxious about the future ( Bry.",
 C.C.1, Phos.? ). Master Kent said, future looks dark to him ~
 looks on the dark side of everything.
 12 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

ii ) Unpardonable crime and sins :
 He feels as if he had commited many unpardonable crimes
and sins when he was young. Master Kent said, as if, he is.
wholly evil.
iii) Realisation of them :
 On realisation of those crimes, he repents. Master Kent
said, pt. broods over it but that hatches new grievances, and
intensifies the symptom. He is eager to redemption of those
crimes and sins, those he has commited since youth.
 Master Kent said, pt. thinks that he has neglected some-thing. Reproach of neg/ected duty. We deserves reproach
in consequence of having neglected duty — is not worthy of
salvation.
iv) Unwanted element :
 As the pt. broods — that makes the pt. to think that he is
an unwanted element in the society. He feels that life is
@ constant burden to him.
v) Melancholia :
 Dr. Farrington said in almost ail cases in which it is simi-limum, there is present of melancholy with disposition to
weep or with a feeling of self-condemnation.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury reported that most important
characteristic is profound melancholia ( Aur.1, C.C.1, Caust.?,
Graph.?, Gels.*, Ign.?, Nat Mur.?, Puls.? ).
 Pt. is sad, despondent, dejested, with jnvo/untary weeping
C Ign.7, Nat Mur.?, Plat.?, Puls.7, R. Tox.?, Sep 7, Aur.?, Bell.*,
Caust.* ), apathetic with complete d/sgust of Ife. Dr. Kent
said suitable in most profound states of melancholia, —pt.
sits and says nothing. Melancholy, feels shateful and
quarre/some.
 Dr. Taicott recommended that sometimes we find religious
melancholia whence constant prayer is noticable.
 Master Kent said, absolute loss of enjoyment in everything.
Constantly expecting bad news, the future looks dark to him
— resulting melancholia.
Note : Master Kent said, Aurum. state of mind is an insanity,
  MENTAL PICTURES 13

dreadful to look upon because of !ts turbulence and melan-choly Terrible melancholy after mercury
vt) Miserable life :
 Life is a constant burden to him, hence to get rid of it, he
constantly dwelis on suicide ( Naja., Nat. S ,— but is afraid
to die, Nux Vom. ). Dr. Farrington said, pt. has suicidal
thoughts, even if pt. does not make actual attempts to suicide
 Dr. Boericke said constantly dwelling on suicide yet fear
of death.
 Dr. E. B. Nash said, in men, it is oftenest in connection
with liver troubles : in women with womb troubles esp. when
enlarged, endurated or prolapsed.
 Master Kent said affections are natural to healthy men—-
but these are perverted. Love Of living, of self protection, is
perverted—longs to die, seeks methods to commit suiside
He mediates upon death, upon suicide. He wants to get out
of the world.
vii) Excessive questioning :
 Dr. Boericke said, excessive questioning without waiting
for reply is another feature of Aur. Met.
vii) Tremendous Oversensitive :
 Our Aurum Met. is exceedingly oversens/tive, a mere noise
in the door makes the pt. anxious.
ix) Aggravations & Ameliorations :
 < from sunset to sun rise.
 < from mental exertion.
 < from melancholic brooding.
 > in the morning ( Clarke ).
x) Low-sspirited :
 Arum Met. pt. is tife-less, pt. feels uneasy, has great desire
for mental and physical activity but can’t do things fast
enough
xi) Life-Less :
 it seems that joyousness of mind is not for Aurum Met.
He is melancholic, depressed, excessive scruples of
conscience. There is aversion to conversation. Dr. Kent said,
  14 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

he wants to destroy himself, has no love for his life which he
thinks worthless.
xii) Inferiority Complex ;
 inferiority complex (— superiority complex, Platina ), is a
grand feature of this medicine.
 Self condemnation is inborn, there is depressive insanity
(+++), hence pt. broods and inferiority complex becomes
evidently marked.
 Master Kent classically explained that continual self-reproach, self-criticism, imagines he can’t succeed in anything
and he does everything wrong—he is in dis-union with
himself. Imagines he sees obstacles in this way everywhere
xiii) Contradiction unbearable :
 Least contradiction excites his wrath (Nash), contradic-tion is unbearable (Aur.', Ign.1, Lyco.1, Sep.1, Bry.?, Coce.?,
N. V.?, Sil.?}}~makes him irritable and excites him. Master
Kent said, every little thing rouses him into anger and turmoil.
Dr. Farrington said any contradiction or dispute excitie$ the
patient furiously, he becomes red in face and his pugnacity
is aroused.
xiv) Unhappy :
 Master Kent gave the picture. Sometimes he is sound in
his business affairs, seems to be an intelligent man but
silently broods over his state and is hatred of the world, tells
nohody of it, thus he becomes unhappy, and thence found
being hang in his room.
Q. The mental picture of ARSENICUM ALBUM.
 { like to impress the mental picture of Arsenic through the
word ‘Fastidious’, as Arsenic. is very fastidious; thus
remember the mental! picture through this word.
 F=— Fear.
 A= Anxious.
 S= Sad.
 T= Time modality.
 t=Incurable disease.
 D= Dreads solitude.
  MENTAL PICTURES 15

 {== Irritable.
 O= Orderly mania.
 U-=Un-natural oversensitive.
 S— Suicidal tendency.
1. Mental causations :
 i) Grief (Ref. Clarke).
 ii) Fright (Ref. Clarke).
 iii) Fit of passion
 iv) Long exposure to malarial influences.
ij. Characters :
 a) Fear:
 Arsenic pt. has feer of death. Master Kent said, dread of
death when alone, or on going to bed. He thinks that he ts
going to die and wants somebody with him.
 Master Kent reported that a sudden anxious fear comes
over him at night, he jumps out of bed with fear that he is
going to die, or that,he is going to suffocate. Sometimes
fear drives him out of bed, he hides in a closet.
Dr. J. H. Clarke said: i) fear of solitude,
 ii) fear of spectres,
 iii} morbid fear of cholera (Nit. Ac ),
 iv) fear of robbers ( Ars.?, Arg. N.?,
 Ign.*, Lach.*, Merc.*, Nat M.?, Phos 2)
Note : Master Kent said, he has violent increase of his fear
and horror in the dark and many complaints come on im the
evening as darkness is coming on.
b) Anxious :
 Master Kent said, t#e anxfety that is found in Arsenic. 7s
intermingled with fear.
 The anxiety takes form also in the restlessness ( it is
restless both mentally and physically, one of the member of
Mash’‘s trio of restless medicines).
 This anxious restlessness has three phases.
 in acute stage, pt. goes from chair to chair, child goes
from nurse to mother, from one’s lap to other.
 Thence an uneasiness comes as this constant change of
  16 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 position makes the patient exhaustsd. Thence he is in bed and
 unable to sit up, thus rolis in bed and thence the prostration
 comes out of position. Exhaustion is not felt while lying still,
 but as soon as he moves, pt is surprised to find himself so
weak. Thus this leads to cadaveric aspect of the pt, when
he lies in bed hke a cadaver
 Thus Master Kent warns us to remember that these state
 of anxiety and restlessness go towards the cadaveric aspect,
towards death. Kent said, at first there is that anxious rest-lessness with fear, but the increasing weakness tends towards
prostration.
 Master Kent also reported another phase of anxiety viz
anxiety like one who has commited murder. He finally works
up to the idea that the officers are coming after him and
watches if they are coming in to arrest him
 Some unusual evil is going to happen — hence he is
anxious.
 Extreme anxiety in the evening in bed, said Master Kent
c) Sad:
 Sadness- prevails to a great extreme Master Kent said,
averse to meeting — because he imagines that he has
formerly offended them. Great menta/ depression, great
sadness, melancholy with despair of recovery. Pt. is so sad
that he is weary of life ; he loathes life and wants to die.
 Dr. Clarke said that great apathy and indifference also
characterizes Ars. Alb.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury said very frequently the insanity
takes the form of religious melancholia characterized by
hopelessness and despairs of his salvation, life holds out no
charm for him—melancholia.
d) Time modality :
 Master Kent reported that many of the mental! troubles
( as well as physical troubles ), come on and increased at
certain times < from 1-2 P. M. and 1-2 A. M. < after
midnight, very soon after midnight his sufferings begins and
1—2 O'clock they are intensified.
  MENTAL PICTURES 17

 e) Incurable disease :
 Pt. thinks that his disease is incurable — his disease is
 fatal and # is useless to take medicine as he is surely going
 to die.
 f) Dreads solitude : ;
 Ars. Alb. pt. dreads solitude. Aversion to being alone
 ( Kali C., Bis., Lyco ) ( —Rev., Ign., Nux Vom. ).
 Master Kent said, pt. dreads solitude and wants company,
 because in company he can talk and put off the fear.
 Dr. Talcott said, fears to be left alone lest he should do
 himself bodily harm.
 g) Irritable :
 Irritability is also a feature of Ars. Alb. Master Kent in
 his repertory kept it in the second grade. Though Kent kept
 it in first grade in the rubric, ailments after anger with anxiety
 (Acon.?, Ign.?, Nux Vom.?).
 h) Orderly mania :
 A morbid fastidjousness has its similimum in Arsenic ( Ref.
 Tyler ).
 Pt. keeps everything in order,—tip-top. These patients
 are hard to please.
 Dr. C. Hering is justified in calling Ars Alb. pt as
“A gold-headed cane patient’.
i) Un-natural Oversensitive :
 Sensitiveness is a feature of Arsenic. Oversensitive to
circumstances, to surroundings of the room_ characterizes
Ars. Alb. (Ref. Tyler).
j) Suicidal tendency :
 Kent reported, Ars pt. does commit suicide It is a remedy
full of suicidal tendencies Suicidal dispositioh esp. at night
and after midnight (Nux Vom ) ( Ref. Kents’ Repertory ).
Suicidal disposition by hanging ( Bell.?, Nat. Sulph *), with

 sometimes with /nclination to commit suicide (Clarke).
 viii) Like April day - changeable mood :
 Dr Nash said that changeability of the symptoms like
 April day.
 One of the characteristic symptom is ch angeableness of
 symptoms (Ign., Nux. M ) is also found in the disposition.
 The patient is now irritable, then tearful again, or mild and
 Pleasant but, even with irritableness is easily made to cry
 Dr. Nash also says we sometimes have patients come into
 the office, and find tn trying to take their case no “head or
 tail’ to it. It is mixed Puls. will often clear up and cures
 the case.
 Dr. Farrington has described the changeableness of mentaf
 symptoms. He said that in the mental symptoms, too, are
 of the same fickle nature, the patient now being irritable, then
 tearful and again mild and pleasant.
 ix) Low spirit—fFear :
 Dr, Clarke reports that Puls. has great fear. Fits of anxiety.
 with fear of death, or of an apoplectic attack, with buzzing in
 ears, shieverings, and convulsive movements of fingers,
 apprehension, anthropophobia. fear of ghosts at night or in
 evening. with an impulse to hide or to run away, mistrust and
 suspicion.
 “As evening comes on, begings to fear ghosts” (Clarke).
 x) Amiable : Dr. Hering gives these additional touches to
 the Puls. type : sandy hair, blue eyes, pale face easily moved
 to laughter or tears, affectionate, mild, timid, gentle, yielding
 disposition, inclined to be fleshy,—easy disposition.
 Notes : 1) Besides this, Dr. Kent says that, it has melancho-lia, sadness, weeping, despair, religious despair, fanatical,
full of notions and whims, imaginative, extremely excitable.
She imagines the company of the opposite sex a dangerous
thing to cultivate. They imagine that certain articles of diet
are not good for the human race. Aversion to marriage is a
strong symptoms. A man takes it into his head that it ts an
 50 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

evil thing to have sexual intercourse with his wife and abs-tains from it ; religious freaks.
 2) Mental calmness indicates Puls.
 (—contra-indicates, Acon. Cham.) (Guernsey).
 3) It is especially applicable to those states of Aypochon-driacal depression preceded or accompained by profuse
 catarrhal discharges, and by inflammatory condition of the
 genital organs in both sexes (Talcott).
 4) Dr. Hering has described Puls pt. fatigued by mental
 labour; after slight ernottons difficult breathing
 ii. Mental Modalities :
 <Evening and night.
 < Twilight.
 <<Alternate evenings.
 <Change of weather.

 Q. Enumerate the mental picture of SULPHUR
 Remember the typical Sulphur mentality through the word
 ‘Philosopher’. As our sagacious personality Dr. Constantine
 Hering has denoted Sulphur pt. as a ‘ragged philosopher’
 —thus the word Philosopher rightly suits to elucidate our
 Sulphur mentality.
 P-=Philosophical mania.
 H==Happy dreams, wakes up singing.
 !=Indifferent.
 L=Loss of memory.
 O=—Opposite of fastidious (Kent).
 S$=—Selfish.
 O—Oversensitive.
 P=Pseudocyesis.
 H=Hypochondriac.
 E== Egoistic.
 R=Religious mania.
 lL. Mental Causations :
 i) Mental Symptoms engrafted in a psoric base after
 suppression of skin eruption.
  MENTAL PICTURES

 ii) Master Kent said persons who lead Sedentary iives,
 confined to their rooms in study, in medication, in philoso-Phical enquiry, and who take no exercise, soon find out that
they must eat only the simplest foods, foods not sufficient to
nourish the body, and they end up by going into a philoso-phical mania.
 iit) Dr Clarke said over-exertion may results various
mental ailments
Hi. Character :
 a) Philosophical mania :
 it was our lamented Dr. C. Hering who called the Sulphur
pt —the ragged philosopher’
 The typical Sulphur scholar, the inventor, works day and
night in thread bare cloths and battered hat, with long uncut
hair and a dirty face Thus Master Kent said he becomes a
false philosopher. Pt, dresses himself with most filthy rags
seems beautiful, he ignorantly wears paper crown and think
himself ‘His Majesty’—the king — such a Philosophical
mania characterizes our Sulphur pt and the more he goes on
in this state the more he is disappointed because the world
does not consider him the greatest man on the earth.
 Master Kent said monomania over the study of strange
and abstract things, occult things, things that are beyond
knowledge.
 In Sulphur behaviour it is not that kind of philosophy that
has a basis and which can be followed up, reasoning ina
series, reasoning on things that are true but a fanatical kind
of philosophy that has no basis — an aversion to systematic
work ~~ i. e., pt is a sort of inventive genius.
 When he gets an idea in his mind he is unable to get rid
of it. He follows it and follows it, until finally accidentaly
he drops it.
Note : 1. Dr. Talcott in his book ‘Mental diseases’ said
that this indulgence in philosophical speculations are followed
by abnormal mental exhaustion.
b) Happy dreams, wakes up singirg,
 This is an uncommon socutigh Beem that Charité
 aey
our Sulphur mentality.
  52 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 Pt. dreams happy visions and suddenly wakes up at mid-night and sings loudly —thence Sulphur will be the drug of
 choice.
 Master Kent in his repertory classed Sulphur tn the follow-ing sub-rubrics :
 i) Anxious dreams ( Acon.*, Am.C.%, Arm ?, Ars.*, Baryta.*,
 C.C.?, Graph.?, Lyco.?, Nat.M.%, Nit.Ac.*, N.V.*, Phos.?,
 Puls.?, R.T.1, Sil., S*., Thuja.* ).
 ii) Upleasant dreams ( Sulph.*, Gels.” ).
 c) Indifferent :
 Our Sulphur pt is indifferent; with sometimes have
 another phase of mentality characterized by aversion to work,
 to business.
 He will sit around and do nothing. Nothings appeals him,
 nothing affords him pleasure.
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury compares the indifference of Sulphur
 with Phosphorus and Sepia. Sulphur has not the indifference
 that is manifested chiefly towards one’s own relations and
 beloved (Phos, Sepia) but it has a disgust for everything
 mundane as he calls it.
 d) Loss of memory :
 Master Kent said, a pt. needing Sulphur often in a state of
duliness and confusion of mind, with inability to collect the
thoughts and ideas, lack of concentration. Pt. can’t find the
Proper word during conversation ( Arn.*, Arg. Nit.*, Lyco.*,
Medo.*, Nat.Mur.2, Nux Vom.*, S.? ).
 Pt. may remember events which has occured tong tong
ago but forgets recent events ( Graph. ).
e) Opposite of fastidious :
 It is again our lamented tiger prescriber and master teacher
Tyler Kent who has compared the reverse order of Sulphur
so far the fastidiousness of Arsenicum is considered. These
two remedies are the extremes of each other in this feature.
 Arsenicum. wants his clothings clean, wants everything
in tip-top manner whereas in our Sulphur pt. cleanliness is
not 2 great idea, he thinks it is not necessary. He is dirty but
it does not worry him.

MENTAL PICTURES 53

 He is totally untidy, the Sulphur student will leave the
books piled up in an indiscriminate manner, there ts no order
—a state of untidiness and uncieanliness. He put on a shirt
that has worn many weeks, he would wear his shirt untill tt
fell of from him.
Note : 1.
 Master Kent said, Sulphur ts se/dom indicated in a cleanly
people—but itis commonly indicated in those who are not
disturbed by uncleanliness
Note : 2.
 Dr. Kent said, after medication with Sulphur an /ndividual
begins to take notice of himself and puts ona clean shirt,
whereas his early appearances were in the one same old
shirt.
f) Selfish :
 Sulphur viétiates his affections. driving him to a most
marked state, of se/fishness. He has no thoughts of any
pody’s wishes or desires. Everything that he contemplates is
for the benifit of himself. There is absence of gratitude.
This state of selfishness runs through the Sulphur patient.
g) Oversensitive :
 Master Kent reported that Sulphur pt. is oversens/tive to
filthy odors. But he eats filthy substances,—the child is
subjected to catarrhal discharges and he often eats the nasal
discharge
 The oversensitiveness to filthy odors is marked as he
becomes nauseated even from the odor of his own body.
The odor of the stool is so offensive that it will follow him
around ali day.
h) Pseudocyesis :
 There is a feeling of movement in abdomen as of a child
€ Corc., Nux. Mos,, Thuja. ) - this is a feature of false preg-nancy i.e, pseudocyesis.
i) Hypochondriac :
 Sulphur. is Aypochondriacal in nature with nervous
disposition.
 54 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 Dr. C. Hering said, hypochondriac mood throughout the
day ; merry in the evening.
p> Egoistic :
 Sulphur is egojstic in his disposition, everything that he
contemplates is for the benifit of himself
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury said, :f there is anything to which he
attaches any importance, it is the question of his own
 salvation.
 Dr Constantine Hering reported,—great obstinacy, dislike
to have anyone near him—this also characterizes his egoistic
 mood.
 k) Religions mania :
 This is characterized by refigious melancholy not medi-tating upon the rational religion, but on foolish tdeas-viz, pt.
 meditates on ‘who made God’ ? She could never be con-tended until she found out the man who made itt, and then
 she wanted to Know who was his,father. That is a feature
 of religious maniacal melancholia of Sulphur.
 She also prays constantly and uninterruptedly without
 going out from her room, moaning with despair and thinks
 that she has sinned away her day of grace.

 Q. Enumerate the pen picture of THUJA mentality
 Here | will enumerate the mental picture of Thuja Occi-dentalis through the name of the medicine.
 T=Trickling of urine in urethra, like fixed ideas
 H—=Humourless
 U=Unbearable music
 J (S)==Suicidal mania.
 A =Angry.
 O=Owling to loss of memory—forgetful.
 C=-Control of super-human being (Fixed idea).
 C—=Convex buttom pressed on the head (Fixed tdea).
 t==Insane woman.
 D=-Delicate body (Fixed idea)
 E= Eyes swollen (Fixed tdea).
 N=-Nail driven into parietal bone (Fixed idea).
  MENTAL PICTURES 55

 T=Talks hastily
 A=After chifd-birth mental depression (Causation).
 L=Limbs are of glass : lower limb of wood (Fixed idea)
 j= Irritable
 S=Scull-bone pieces ; strange person at side ;
 stabbed fore-head (Fixed idea).
 Mental Causations :
 1) Bad effects of vaccinaton (Dr Farrington said, imbeci-lity after vaccination).
 it) Psychic diseases results after suppressed or mal-treated gonorrhoea (Medo ), abuse of Sulphur and Mercury.
 ii) Dr Boericke has recommended that complaints from
moon-light
 iv) Mental depression after chiid-birth (Ref. Boericke)
ii, Character :
 a) Trickling of urine in urethra like fixed ideas :
 Our Thuja. pt has got different types of fixed ideas -
 As if
 i) The soul and body were seperated. (Bapt,, Petrol.)
 ii) A strange person is at her side.
 iii) He is under the control of some super human being,
from which he can’t get rid of Dr. N M Chowdhury has
reported that the pt. thinks his hands and feet are bounded.
 iv) She is transparent. (Kent).
 v) She ts delicate, made up of glass, would break easily.
Dr. Farrington said this symptom is a esp, indication in case
of enteric fever.
 vi) As if animal were a crying. motion as if something
alive ; protudes here and there like the arm of foetus (Croc.,
Nux Mos., Sulph.)
 vi) The lower limbs were made up of wood, the sensa-tion comes esp on walking.
 vill) flesh were beaten and scrapped from the bones, Dr.
Clarke said, scalp as if beater.
 ix) A nail has been driven into the right parietal bone
i.e. clavus, and in the left frontal eminence.
 56 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 x) A convex buttom was pressed on the head
 Dr. Clarke reported on the left ear.
 x1) She is made up of brittle substance, so will not allow
anybody to approach her.
 xii) As if vertex was pressed with a needle (Ref. Clarke).
 xiil}) As if fore-haed will fall out, the bones of the head
 has been knocked to pieces.
 xiv) Dr. John Henry Clarke reported that fore-head, ears
 and eyes, as if stabbed.
 xv) As if fine sands are put on the eyes, or foreign body
 in the eye,
 Notes : Dr. Farrington said, these fixed ideas are not due
 to an irritability of the mind that drives everyone away, but
 here it is a fixed delusion.
 b) Humour-less :
 Depression of spirit, resulting dissatisfaction is marked
 over his.entire feature. Dr. Clarke said pt. is sad, ill humoured.
ec) Untearable music :
 Music is unbearable, makes her to weep ( Graph.*,
 Kreos.*, Nat. C.?, Thuja.* ). pt. may have trembling of feet on
 hearing the music.
 d) Suicidal Mania :
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury reported that sometimes Thuja. pt.
 exhibits a peculiar type of su/cidal disposition (Dr. Kent in
 Repertory Kept it in third grade under the subrubrics, suicidal
 disposition and thoughts of suicide) whence pt. attempts to
jump out of the window.
e) Angry :
 Overexcitation, getting vexed at trifles is another feature
 of Thuja. mentality.
 f) Owing to loss of memory—forgetful :
 Pt. is forgetful, owing to /oss or weakness of memory.
 Master Kent in his Repertory classed Thuja. in first grade in the
rubric, —'mistakes word in writing’ ( Lach.!, Lyco.?, Am.C.?,
Nat. Mur.*, N.Mos.? ).
g) Insane woman :
 Insane woman will not be touched or approached.
  MENTAL PICTURES 57

 h) Talks hastily :
 Master Kent in his Repertory graded Thuja. in second grade
 in the sub-rubric, hasty speech (Hep.?, Hyos?, Lach.},
 Merc.)
 Ii. Modalities : < in night and during increasing sun
 ( Ref. Clarke ).
 Q. State the mental picture of VERATRUM ALBUM.
 1 will impress you the mental picture of Veratrum Album
 through the name of the medicine.
 V==Violent mania
 E=Excitement.
 R=Religious mania.
 A=Anxiety - attempts to suicide.
 T= Thinks pregnant.
 R= Restless.
 U= Unbearable, if left alone.
 M-= Melancholia.
Il. Mental Causations :
 i) Disappointed love (Caust, Nat M, I[gn., Aur.M.,
Ant. C., Lach, Calc. Phos ).
 ii) Fright.
 ii) }=Shock.
 iv) Injured pride or honour (Ref. Clarke & Hering).
il. Characters :
 a) Violent mania :
 Due to cerebral congestion we find in our Veratrum Alb.
pt. there is an outburst of violent mania like Belladonna.
 Master Kent said, the mental symptoms are marked by
violence and destructiveness; he wants to destroy, to tear
the clothes from the body.
 Pt. strikes those around him (Belt, Stramo.) —a state of
violency. :
Note. 1: Pt. always wants to be busy, te carry on this daily
work. a
 Note. 2 * Master Kent said, those biowed down by great
grief and despair are likely to go into a state of violénmt mania.
 58 Syneptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

b) Excitement—Lascivious—>Nymphomaniac :
 There is violent sexual mania characterized by Lascivious-ness (Hyos.', Lach.*, Lil. Tig.1, Phos.1, Platina.*, Staph.*)
resulting either aymphomania (in females) or satyriasis
Cin males ).
 Dr. Kent said, pt. howls, sings obscene songs, exposes to
the persons. Lewdness and lascivious talks. DOr. Kent also
recommended a state of loquacity.
 Dr. Clarke said, abusive language on slightest provocation.
Lechery and obscene talks, kisses everybody. Pt. exhibits
 immodesty, exposes his private parts, kicks the clothes and
 becomes naked
 — such a disordered state can be brought
 into order by our Veratrum., provided totality corroborates.
 Dr. Hering said ‘k/sses every body’ this disposition comes
 esp. before menses.
 c) Religious mania :
 Pt. is praying and beseeching ail the time without respite.
 Master Kent classicaily explained this exalted state of reli-gious frenzy. Master Kent said, praying for hours, thinks he
 is ‘risen Christ’
 @) Anxiety—Attempts to suicide :
 Master Kent in his Repertory classed it in first grade under
 the rubric ‘anxiety’ ( Acon.?, Arg.N.?, Ars.?. Aur.?, Bell 1,
 Bry.*, ©.Veg.", Caust.?, Nit.Ac.?, Puls’, Phos.?, RhusTox.?,
 Secale.*, Sulph.?, V.A.* ). ‘Anxiety about salvation’ ( Ars.*,
 Lach.?, Lil. Tig.4, V.A.1 ). This anxiety of mind leads to fear
 of death whence pt. attempt to suicide. Suicidal disposition
 through windows (Aur.?, Aeth.*, Glon.*, V.A.?) Dr. Kent
 explained despair of his recovery leads him to this suicidal
 disposition. Dr. Clarke said, tired of life, but fear to die.
 Dr. Clarke said suicidal tendency from religious despair.
 Dr. Constantine Hering explained that, despair of his
 position in society, feels very unlucky—despai: of salvation.
 6) Thinks pregnant :
 Pt. thinks she is pregnant ( Thuja., Sabad.) and will soon
 be delivered. This is characterized by puerperal mania
(Cimicifuga).
  MENTAL PICTURES 59

 Dr. Talcott said, even lady of 80-390 years of age fancies
herself pregnant.
¥) Restless :
 Dr. Farrington in his Clinical Materia Medica elucidated
that the delirium of Verat. Alb. is associated with restlessness-with three characteristic mania, violency, loquacity and
jasciviousness.
g) Unbearable, if left alone :
 Dr. Clarke said, unbearable if left alone Does not wants
to be alone, yet persistently refuses totalk If he talks, he
scoids.
 Dr. E. B. Nash said, dispose to talk about fault of others
or becomes silent.
 Or. Talcott said, sometimes pt. inclined to gossip but find
out faults of others, scotds them.
h) Melancholia :
 A state of breoding is aiso a characteristic feature. Pt. is
full of despair and hopelessness Master Kent said, sits
and broods in silence with head hangs down. There is
sulfen indifference.
 Pt. thinks he was a man of great importance proud of his
 position, but now despair of his position in the society hence
 profound melancholia results. Dr. Clarke said, pt. never
 smiles—such a melancholic state characterizes our Veratrum
 Alb. pt.
 Dr. Clarke said, melancholy, dejection, sadness with
 inchnation to weep. inconsolable affliction. with howlings
 and cries on account of imaginary misfortunes.
 ill. Modalities : <from fright, <before and during menses
 ( Ref. Clarke ).
 Note. 1: Master Kent said, a few such remedies would empty
 our insane asylums of recent cases. insanity is curable if
 there are no incurable results of the disease.
Note. 2: Whenever we find the manias as described in
 Veratrum pt. are present or they succeeds one another—give
 60 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

the medicine, and that is Veratrum Album ; the drug of choice.
Note, 3: Our immortal Master Hahnemann said, Veratrum
Album. had power to promote cure of almost one third of
insanes of the lunatic asylum.
  CHAPTER—2

 GUIDING SYMPTOMS

ACONITUM NAPELLUS
 As Master Kent said rheumatism or facial neuraigia comes
on from the dry cold wind, —thus let us imagine of a man,
driving his car in the ‘week-end’ to enjoy the week-end
holidays but due to exposure to dry cold-wind, facial neu-ralgia results ; —-hence let us consider Aconite as a week-end
remedy and we will take up the tips, Friday and Saturday as
week-end, thus through this tips allow me to enumerate the
guiding symptoms of Aconite.
F== Fear. S=Sanguine temperament
R=-Restlessness with sedantary life
I==Intansity of action. A=<Active haemorrhage.
D=Dry & hot skin T==Tension.
A=< & >. U=Unquenchable thirst.
Y=Yielding ailments. R=Red face becomes pale.
 (*Here Day is common).
 1. Fear :-Great fear and anxiety of mind with great
nervous excitability is the characteristic of Acon. patient.
Afraid to go out, to go into a crowd where there is any
excitement of many people’ it has got fear of death in acute
disease, fear of darkness (Caust.), fear of ghost, fear to cross
the street ( Arg. Nit. ), fear to cross a bridge, fear of death in
pregnancy. Fear of future Fear of the fright remains ( Op.,
Stramo. ). Life is rendered miserable for Acon. patient due té
fear. He is sure his disease wit prove fatal, predicts the day
and moment of death.
 2. Restlessness :- Acon. patient is restfess, ‘anxious,
does everything in a great haste, must change pesition ato,
everything startles him. :
 It is one of the Nash’s‘trios of. restless: medicines{ otfvets
being Arsenic: & Rhustox).-
 62 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

 Acon is restless mentally
 (—Rhus Tox. is restless physically. Arsenic is restless both
physically & mentally). Acon. patient is impatient and his
 impatience makes him restless ( Ref. Dr N. M. Chowdhury ).
Aconite pains are intolerable. It is also one of the Nash’s
trio of greatest pain remedy (others are Chamomiila and
Coffea).
 They drive him crazy, patient becomes restiess at night,
due to this pain, with agony and mental anxiety. Our
immortal Master Hahnemann says, “Whenever Aconite is
chosen homoeopathically you must, above ali, observe
the moral symptoms, and be careful that it closely resembles
them, the anguish of mind and body, the restiess ness, the
disquiet not to be allayed.”
 Note. : it is interesting to note that Master Kent In his
 Repertory classed Acon. in first grade, under sub-rubic, aver-sion to motion ( Acon.’, Ars.;, Bell.?, Bry.t, Cale.1, Lach *,
 NuxVom.', Ruta.?, Sil.1, Sulph.?, Baryta.?, CarboVeg.?, China ?,
 Gels.?, Graph.*, Lyco.*, Nat.Mur.?, Thuja.” ).
3. Intensity of action :
 Acon is indicated in the first stage of any acute disease
 which starts suddenly and viofently like a storm
 Dr. Kent says that the patient seems to be threatened with
 a sudden and violent death, but recovery is quick. So. as
 was observed by Dr. Dunhum, it is like a great storm.
 Dunham’s discussion of this remedy in his Materia Media is
 very poetical. It has got no periodicity, nor any wave ( Ref
 Tyler ).
 Note. 1: -Acon. is the acute of Sulphur and both precedes
and foliows it in acute inflammatory conditions.
 Note. 2: Acon. is the drug for the congestive stage of
 inflammation before localisation takes place (Ref. Nash)
4. Dry and hot Skin :
 Dry and hat skin with rare sweat (Nash). There is dren-ching sweat, especiatly on parts laid on, ( Master Kent in his
 Repertory classed, ‘perspiration on the affected parts. Ambra.’,
 Ant.T.?, Merc.?, Rhus Tox.1). which relieves (Boericke) (Nat.
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 63

Mur., Psor.), (Master Kent in his Repertory said, symptoms
ameliorates while sweating, Bry.*, Cup.?, Gels.1, Nat. Mur.?,
Rhus Tox.*, Acon.%, Ars.?, Chamo.*, Graph,*, Lach.®, Hep.?,
Thuja.*, Verat.?).
 Note : Cold sweat, icy coldness of face may be observed
in Acon. patient. It is mostly found in febrile condition
5. Aggravation & Amelioration :
 <in the evening.
 <at night.
 <in the warm room
 >by uncovering
 >in the open air. (Afum., Mag.C., Puls., Sab.).
6. Yielding ailments :
 Acon. diseases caused by exposure to dry cold ajr (Ars.,
Chamo., Camph., Caust., Rumex., Sil., Hepar., Psor., China.),
dry north or west wind or exposure to draught of cold air, bad
effects of checked perspiration (Bellis, Duic., Rhus Tox,
Baryta Carb.), fear, fright. shock, heat of the sun, excitement,
injury, surgical operation etc.
Note. 1 : Paralysis from exposure to dry cold wind (acute
effect) (—chronic effect, Caust.).
 Note. 2: Master Kent said, complaints come on sud-denly from the very cold weather of winter or from the intense
hot weather of summer.
7. Sanguine temperament with sedentary life. -
 It is generally indicated in acute or recent cases occuring
in young persons, especially girls of a full, plethoric habit
who lead a sedentary life >; persons easily affected by atmos-pheric changes, dark hair and eyes, rigid muscular fibre and
of sanguine temperament (quick in action and perception).
8. Active haemorrhage :
 It has got active haemorrhage from any part of the body
both internal and external ; uterus or other places in stout
Plethoric patients. The character of the blood is pure, and
bright red, accompained by fear of death and nervous excita-bility. (Master Kent classed Acon. under second grade, in the
rubric, haemorrhage under generalities, Acon.*, Bell.*, Cale.,
 64 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

Carbo Veg.*, China.*, Crot.*, Fer *, Ham.', Ipec.1, Lach.!, Merc.
Cor.?, Mill.*, Nat. Mur.?, Nit. Ac.1, Nux Vom,?, Phos 7, Puls.?,
 Sabina.?, Sec.?, Sulph.?, Apis.?, Arg. N.?, Bry.*, Chamo.?,
 Dulc.?, Graph.*. Psor.*, Rhus Tox ®, Sil ®, Tril 7).
 9. Tension .
 Dr. Huge says *‘Tension’”’ is the kKey-note of Aconite
 patient (—key-note of Belladonna is congestion).
 Due to irritation of mind and affection of circulation,
 tension always prevails in Acon. patient.
 N. B. Aconite causes turmoil tn circulation, Belladonna causes
 turmoil in brain and Chamomiulla cause turmoil in tempera-ment. These three are the Dr. CLARKE’S A.B.C. of nurseries.
 10. Unquenchable thirst :
 Unquenchable thirst for targe quantity of cold water
 is the characteristic symptom of Acon. Everything tastes bitter
 except water (Kent) (Stan.).
 N. 8. Desire for bitter things (Dig., Nat.M., Tereb.}(Ref. Lippe)
 11. Red face becomes pale :
 The face of Aconite is red or red and pale alternately—
 anxious & frightened expression Sensation of face growing
 or swelling on rising from a recumbent position, the red face
 becomes deathly pale or he becomes faint or giddy and falls,
 and he fears to rise again, often accompanied by vanishing
 of sight and unconsciousness. !t is mostly found in febrile
 condition.
 APIS MELLIFICA :
 Know the totality of Apis Mel through Apis Mel.
 A= Ailments from.
 P==Pains.
 1=Incontinence of urine
 S=Sensitiveness.

 M= Most jealous.
 E=Extremities are dropsical.
 L=Laek of thirst.
 1. Ailments from :
 Ailments from jealousy, fright, rage, vexation, bad-news,
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 65

grief ( Ref Clarke). Bad effects of acute exanthema —imper-fectly developed or suppressed (Zinc ), from measies, scarlatina,
 urticaria, etc.
 2. Pains :
 Dr. E B Nash said, ‘It seems to me that in this remedy
 also the leading characteristic ts to be found in its sensation
—burning, sunging pains’ They are sharp and quick, Iike the
sting of the bee These pain are characteristic of this remedy
These pains suddenty migrating from one part to other (Kal: B1.,
Kali. S., Mag. Phos, Lac.Can., Phyto., Puls, Mang.Ac.). The
pains may be of burning character and aggravated by heat
( Suiph ).
3 Incontinence of urine .
 Apis has /ncontinence of urine, with great irritation of the
 parts, can scarcely retain the urine a moment, and when
 passed scalds severely; frequent, painfut, scanty bloody urt-nation. Master Kent said much _ straining before the urine
will start, and then only a few drops, —strangury, agony in
vioding urine ; retention of urine in nursing infants
Note Increased flow of urine shows it is having a favour-able effect (Ref Clarke).
4 Sensitiveness :
 Extreme sensrtiveness to touch ( Apis?, Bell.t, China’,
Hep.', Lach, Merc?, Petrol.?, Phos Ac}, Plb.?, Sil.?,
Sulph ') Dr Clarke said, general soreness
 —— every pain is
painful to contact. This sensitiveness and sorness is also

extremities, from nervous excitement, from hysterical manifes-tations and an unusually increased flow of menstrual blood,—

8. Ulcers :
 Our sagacious Kent reported that everywhere we find

 3. Splinter sensation :

 Dr. Allen also reported of the sensation of spinter in or about
 uterus when walking or riding.
 10. Tremor :
 Dr. Clarke said tremor is among the leading symptoms

 11. Imperfect co-ordination of muscles :
 Dr. Clarke said this imperfect or defective co-ordination

 Retention or incontinence of urine after labor (Opium) is

 Master Kent said, a general feature of this remedy is that

 Master personalities always explains such symptons im

N.B.: Dr. Hering described Arsenic pt. as “the gold headed
cane patient.”"
2. Restlessness :
 Mentally restless, but physically too weak to move, can’t
rest in any place. Charging place continually, wants to be
moved from one bed to another.
 So, Arsenic patient is restless both mentally & physicalty,
(—Rhus Tox. patient is restless physically and Acan. patient

 72 Synoptic Mlemorizer of Materia Medica

 These are the WNash’s trio of restless medrcines. Dr.

in any other medicine’. Br. Guernsey said that the greater
the suffering the greater the anguish, restlessness, and fear

N. B. : Arsenic patient can be compared with the race of
horse as Antim crud to swine and Pulsatilla to the race of
sheep. Dr. John Henry Clarke rightly said, as the horse is
exceedingly nervous animal, constantly moving about, restless
to a degree and very prone to take fright — quite a picture of
Arsenic temperament.

3. Severe prostration :
 Great prostration, with rapid sinking of the vital force,
fainting, exhaustion. Drawing pain between the scapulae,
which compels him to lie down —‘the perspiration exhausts
him as he lies in bed, almost to the production of syncope
etc.” Hahnemann gives us avery important footnote, “That
symptoms of a not very important character and otherwise,
trivial affections induce a sudden and complete sinking of
the strength, is a very important and characteristic peculiarity

4. Excessive burning ; Excessive thirst :

 b) Great thirst for cold water, drink often hut tittle ata

Bell
2. Redness :
 As a result of severe inflammatory process which when
tends to localize, as Dr Nash said, Belladonna im the first stage

are red inflammed areas either localized in parts or a general
redness —- reminds us to think of Beiladonna, the drug of

3. Heat :
 As a result of inflammatory reaction heat is produced
and Beil rescues such cases. Skin jis hot, imparts a
burning sensation to examining hand Dr Harvey Farrington
said in febrtble condition, fever sometimes runs high upto

4. Burning :
 Burning is another denoting feature of our Belf Master
Kent said, “‘/itense burning. the burning in the throat with
Bell., — sore throat is Itke a coal of fire.’ Burning Iike fire.
The skin burns — Master Kent masterly depicted the picture
— Pt. says — ‘it burns so, doctor, it burns so’.
5. Dryness :
 Dryness is a characteristic feature — dryness of mucous
membrane of mouth, dryness in everywhere, characterizes Bell.
6. Pains :
 it is one of our /eading pan remedies. The charecteristic

attacks, causes redness
 of face and eyes, fullness of head
and throbbing of carotids. Dr. Clarke saiti, pains of

Bell. run downwards i.e. away from the head ( —Sil. and Gels.
have a pain running up the back ) ( Ref. Clarke )
7. Sensitiveness :
 Dr. John Henry Clarke said it ts a medicine which has
great genera/ .sensitiveness, and also sensitiveness of the
special senses — sensitive to light, to motion, to jars—when
some one touches the bed. Master Kent explained it as
nervous hyperaesthesia.

8. Sleepy but can not sleep :
 Our Bell. is sleepy but can not sleep ( Caust., Chamo.,
Stramo., Opium). Master Kent said, restless sleep; starts in a
sleep as if frightened

 Dr. E. B. Nash said another very valuable modafity can

 6.Irritable :
 Master Kent said, Bryonia has an extreme state of
irritability, which is as extreme as that found in Nux Vom..or

 Due to dryness of all the mucous surfaces, Bryonia. pt.

 Calcarea Carb. is a chilly pt. Pt is sens/tive to cold,
damp air: great fiabiity to take cold. Master Kent graded
Calc. Carb. in second grade in the sub-rubric, tendency to take
cold (Acon.*, Baryta +, Bry.?, Chamo.*, Duic.?, Hep.*, Lyco.!,

RhusTox.*?, Sulph.*7) Master Kent in his Materia Medica said,
sensitive to the coming of a strom, sensitive to coming of
cold weather and when weather changes from warm to cold,
seems imposible for him to keep warm.
2. Anti-psoric :
 it is one of our immortal Master Hahnemann’‘s trio of antr-psoric. Trios are — Sulphur, Calc Carb. and Lycopodium.
3. LtLeucophiegmatic
 Stedmans’ Medical dictionary elaborated the term or
etymology as —a temperament or constitution marked by
pallor of skin. slow and shallow respiration, sluggish circula-tion, hyperplasia of the lymphatic glands — tt is much the
same as the scrofulous diathesis
 Calcarea Carb. 1s of leucophlegmatic constitution with
disposition to grow fat, tendency to obesity in youth ( Am.
Carb., Graph. ), easily tired ; psoric constitution.
4. Coldness :
 Calcarea Carb. has coldness in general and in single parts
( Kali. Bi. ) Master Kent in his Repertory said, coldness in
inner parts ( Calc.*, Lauro.” ).
5, Affection of glands :
 Master Kent said, another marked feature running through
the remedy is its tendency to attack glands, — the glands of
the neck, all the glands of the body —especially the /ymp/hatic
glands. This is a condition characterized by pre-tubercutar
and cancerous manifestations.
6, Ravenous hunger .
 Dr. Clarke said our Calcarea Carb. pt. has ravenous hunger.
Hunger and feeling of emptiness immediately after a meal, and
in the early mornig. Dr. Clarke elucidated the idea—as if the
Pt.does not have the breakfast at proper, time headache comes
on. Master Kent graded Calc. Carb. in second grade in the
rubric, ravenous appetite soon after eating (Cina.*, lod.*, Lyc.7,
Phos.2, Calc.”, Psor.?, Suiph.*} Emaciation and marasmus with
revenous appetite (Calc.*, fod.*, Nat. Mur.*, Abrot.?, Sulph. 7).
But it is to note that, Kent classed Calc. Carb, in first grade

under the sub-rubric ravenous, canine, excessive, increased
appetite ( Am.c.*. Arg. M.1, Ars.7, Calc.?, Calc. Ph.7, China.?,

Sulph.?, Sil.2, V.A.+).
 This appetite is also characterized by craving for indiges-tible things, chalk, coal, etc. (Alumina., Cina., Cicuta., Nit. Ac,
Psor.).
7, Excessive sour discharges :
 Calcarea’s discharges are characterized by excessive sour-ness,—sour vomiting, sour stool, sour diarrhoea—even the
whole body smells sour (Hep., Mag Carb., Rheum.).
 Dr. Clarke said, even the faste of Calc. is sour
8. Assimilation altered :
 Diseases arising from aitered or defective assimilation
(Baryta., Sil.). Dr. Clarke explained it—improper nutrition and
imperfect digestion resulting imperfect osstfication, difficulty tn
learning to walk or delayed mile stones. (—late learning to
walk due to mental dwarfism, Baryta Carb. ; —-due to weak
ankles, Sil —due to nervous weakness, Caust.).
9. Congestion :
 Master Kent said, Calcarea is full of congestions ; — determi-nation of blogd to the head with hot head ; congestion of the
chest, of various parts.
 10, Aversion to meat :
 Our Calcarea has aversion to meat (Calc.*, China.*,
Graph.*, Mur. Ac.?, Nux Vom.!, Petrol.?, Puls.t, Sep.4, Sil +4,
 Sulph.1, Alunima.*, Arn.?, Ars.?, Bry.?, Kali Bi.*, Lyco.3, Nat.
Mur.?, Phos.?, Rhus Tox.*, Tuber.* ). Master Kent classed
aversion to coffee (Calc.7, Nux Vom.*).
11. Relaxation :
 Qur sagacious Master Kent said, Calc. has great relaxation
of the tissues everywhere ; relaxation of muscles, relaxation
of veins, relaxation of the walls of blood-vessels to a great

 1. Left sided :
 Left sidedness of complaints and the d/rection /s left to
 tight. Symptoms begin on the left side and either remain
 there or proceeds to the right ( Ref - Clarke )
 Left side principally affected —left ovary, left testicle, !aft
 chest
 Diphthertc membrane appears in the throat, spreading from
 left to right ( Ref : Kent )
 2. Aggravation from sleep ;: Amelioration from
 discharges, -:
 Dr. Clarke said, ‘‘sleeps into an aggravation ; <after sleep
 whether by day or night as soon as he faifs asleep, the
 breathing stops” (Am.C. Grind., Lac C., Op.).
 Dr. Nash said, patient says “Doctor, if | could only keep
 awake ! would never have another attack’’.
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 97

 Dr. Kent remarked, as soon as the patient goes into sleep
he rouses up with palpitation, with dyspnoea, with suffoca-tion, with exhaustion, with vertigo, with pain in the back of
the head, and many other circularory disturbances.
 Dr. Clarke said that > from the onset of discharges (Zinc)
esp. headache, uterine pain > from nasal discharges &
menses, respectively.
 The other side of this. < from non-appearance of an ex-~
pected discharge.
 Dr. Kent described the menstrual suffering are increased
before and after the flow, with amelioration during the flow.
Note. 1: Dr. Clarke has discussed that the presence of
opposite condition (te > after sleep) does not contrain-dicate Lach. Wants to close the eyes with the headache,
which is > by sleep.
3. Climacteric ailments :
 It is esp. useful at menopause,—menopausal syndrome.
 Climacteric ailments : haemorrhoids, haemorrhages, hot
flushes and hot perspiration ; burning vertex, headache, esp.
at or after the menopause ( Sang., Sulph. ).
 Women who have not recovered from the change of life
“have never felt well since that time” (Ref : Allen’s Keynotes).
Note 1: Blue and purple colour is the characteristic of
Lach. esp. in heart diseases. { Ref. Tyler). It can be coined
that the presence of this colour is monopoly symptom in
favour of Lachesis.
4. Haemorrhagic diathesis :
 Haemorrhagic diathesis ; small wounds bleed easily and
profusely ( Crot., Kreos., Phos., China., Ham., Sec.Cor., Ipec.,
Carb.Veg., Nit.Ac., ).
 The haemorrhages of Lach. have this pecularity — they
contain flakes of docomposed blood, looking like charred
wheat straw. Uterine haemorrhages tn typhoid fever presen-ting these characters will find similimun in Lach. (Ref. Clarke).
5. Exhaustion and trembling :
 Great physical and mental exhaustion, trembling in the
whole body, would constantly sink down from weakness ;
worse in the morning ( Sulph., Tub. }. Tremor of the tongue
is a leading feature of Lach ( Ref : Clarke ).
 98 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

6. Sensitiveness, suspicious & jealous, loquacious :
 Great sensitiveness to touch; throat, stomach, abdomen ;
can’t bear bed clothes or night-dress to touch throat or
abdomen, this is not because of soreness or tenderness
as in Apis. or Bell, but clothes causes an uneasiness, makes
her nervous
 Dr. Clarke said In uterine affections the patient wants to lift
the clothes up, to prevent contact with lower abdomen
Touching the throat in laryngeal affections causes suffocative
spasms.
 Dr. Kent said that the vision becomes very intense, the
hearing becomes intense, the sense of touch esp, becomes
over-wrought ... the patient becomes extremely sensitive
throughout all the senses of the body. The over sensitiveness
to touch ts probably extensively tn the skin ... the mere touch
of the skin with the finger or hand ts unbearable.
 Lach woman is very jealous and suspicious
 Great Loguacity ( Agar, Stram, Hyos.) is marked in Lach
patient ; jumps from one idea to another, one word often
leads into another story.
7. Inside ball — sensation :
 There is a very characteristic symptom in the bladder;
felt esp sensation as ifa baliis rolling loose in the bladder
or abdomen, on turning over. ( Ref. Clarke ).
Note. 1: Besides this, burning sensation and pains are also
leading features throughout this remedy.
Note. 2: Sense of constriction is present in Lach. viz;
throat, heart etc.
8. Slow fanning desires :
 The least thing coming near mouth or nose interferes with
breathing, wants to be fanned, slowly and at a distance
(~rapidly, Carbo.Veg).
LYCOPODIUNM

through the common name of the medicine ie. ‘Club-Moss’
 C=Canins hunger.

J. Canine hunger :
 Canine hunger : The more he eats, the more he craves;
headache if he doesn’t eat.
 Dr. Kent said that Lyco. patient says “everything | eat turns
into wind’. After a mere mouthful he becomes flatulent and
distended, so that he can’t eat any more. He says a mouthful
fills him upto the throat.
 Dr. Kent also said that oysters seems to be poison to Lyco.
patient, just as onions to Thuja patient and the strawberries
to Oxalic Acid pt.
 According to Master Kent this hunger can be aptly dis-cussed in three phases; 1) eating increases the hunger:
ii) canine hunger, but few mouthful feel upto the throat :
ili) aggravation after eating.
2 Lt. foot cold, right foot hot, —leading right sided :
 Text says, “one foot hot and the other cold‘’ (China., Dig.,
Ipec ), is the characteristic of Lyco. patient.
 Dr. Kent illustrated that a child whose left foot is cold and
the other warm with capricious appetite and great thirst yet
losing steadily— give the drug—he'll be cured.
 Again Dr Kent said in the throat symps_ that the right foot
is cold and the left is warm.
 Dr. Clarke reports burning pain like rad-hot coals between
scapulae. (Phos.). (-—burning pains>by heat, Ars}. Burning,
stinging in breasts.
 Dr. Clarke have discussed the key-note is in direction,—
right to left. Any affection commencing on the right side and
spreading to the left (——opp., Lach.) is likely requires Lyco.,
wheather it be headache, sore-throat. chest affection, abdomi-nal affection, pain in ovaries etc.
 Dr. Kent said that there is a predominance of symptoms on
 the right side of the body, and they are likely to travel from
 100 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

right to left or from above down-wards eg from head to the
chiest.
3. Urine—red sand like particles present -
 Red sandin urine, onchild‘s diaper (Phos,) child cries
before urinating (Bor.).
 Aching in kidneys <before, and> after urinating, (Ref.
Clarke).
4. Bloating :
 Lyco. is adapted in gastric affections : excessive accumu-lation of flatulence, good appetite, constant sensation of
satiety, but a few mouthfuls fills upto the throat and he feels
bloated.
 it is one of the trio of tympanitic & flatulent drugs of
Dr, £. B. Nash, others are China & Carbo. Veg., In case of
Lycopodium the lower part of abdomen is full of gas and
distended. (—but the whole abdomen, China :—upper abdo-men, Carbo. Veg).
 Dr. Kent says the noise of the crackling of paper, ringing of
of bells or slamming of door goes through him and causes
fainting. Little things annoys and cause distress Abdomen
is distended like a drum, so that he can hardly breathe.
 This fullness, /s not>by belching (China). Dr E B. Nash
said, with Lyco pt. this flatulent condition is very apt to occur
 in connection with chronic liver troubles Rumbling and fla-tujent is often found particularly in the region of the splenic
flexure.
5. Modalities :
 < From 4to8 P.M esp. in gouty attacks, in rheumatic
fevers, in inflammatory canditions, in pneumonia, in acute
catarrh ( Ref . Kent ).
 The grand characteristic of Lyco. is becoming worse in
this fixed time.
Note : Dr. Kent have discussed the pains are ameliorated from
warmth except head and spine.
6. Oversensitiveness :
 <From 4 to 8 P.M. esp. in gouty attacks, in rheumatic
fevers, in inflammatory conditions, in pneumonia, in acute
catarrh (Ref : Kent).
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS

 The grand characteristic of Lyco ts becefning worse in
 this fixed time
 Dr Kent have discussed the pafns are ameliorated from
 warmth except head and spine
 Dr Kent said that externally there is sensitiveness to a
 warm atmosphere, when there are head and spine symptoms,
 as those are aggravated.
 Dr Clarke said great sensitiveness in liver region esp., in
 case of right-sided sciatica, the patient can’t bear to lie on
 painful side itis so sensitive. Gums, epigastrium, abdomen,
 right side of chest, eruption round the arms; all soft parts
are sensitive.
 Touch and pressure <.
 Note : Text says the patient weeps all day, can’t calm herself,
very sensitive, even cries when thanked
 Dr. Clarke said can't bear any strong smell; can’t endure
noise.
7. Sourness of discharges, suitability :
 Everything tastes sour, eructations, heartburn, water brash,
sour vomiting Thus the sourness of discharges is the charac-teristic of Lyco. patient
 Dr. Clarke, the one of the pioneer of the homoeopathic
world has said, “It is particularly suited to—persons of keen
intellect, but feeble muscular development, upper part of the
body becomes wasted, lower part semi-dropsical, lean and
predisposed to lung and hepatic conditions, herpetic and
scrofulous constitutions, hypochondriac, subjected to skin
diseases. lithic and uric acid diathesis “’
 Dr Kent said, Lyco is anti-psoric, anti-syphilitic and anti-sycotic & its sphere is broad & deep.
 ft is one of the trio of Master Hahnemann’s antipsoric
remedies ( others being Sulph, and Calc. Carb
8. Sweet desires :
 4102 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

that Lyco. has > from warm drinks, though sometimes
> from cold drinks ( throat ).
Note : The patient hates coffee and meat.
MERCURIUS SOLUBILIS HAHNEMANNI
 As you know Mercurius Solubilis Hahnemanni is famous
amongst us as Merc. Sol, thus fet us study the guiding
features of this king of the anti-syphilitic through the name
 of the medicine.
 M-== Modalities.
 E= Every little injury suppurates
 R=Rt sided affections.
 C=Chilly.

 $—Salivated tongue with thirst
 O=Offensive discharges ; offensive sweat.
 L=Leading tremor remedy.
 1. Modalities :
 Dr. Clarke discussed the grand characteristics of the
 ramedy : “as the thermometer is sensitive to changes either
 hot or cold, so is the Mercurius patient has both < by heat
 and < by cold.
 Next very important modality is : < at night ie., sun set
 to sunrise or in other words twilight to dawn aggravation.
 This is a strong point of correspondence with syphilis.
 Note 1: It is esp. noticeable in the bone pains.
 Note 2 . Merc. is Hahnemann’'s typical antisyphilitic remedy,
 as Sulph, is the typical antipsoric and Thuja, the typical
 antisycotic. But by this, it does not mean that they do not
 cover the other miasms, as for example, Dr. J. H. Clarke said,
 ‘Merc. has relation to psora and sycosis as well as syphilis.’
 < in warmth of bed.
 < while sweating.
 <. by lying on rt side.
 Note : Dr H.C. Allen points out that, Merc. has < by heat
 of bed, > from rest in bed: Ars. < from rest in bed > by
 heat of bed.
