chapters.content:
GUIDING SYMPTOMS 103

 2. Every little injury suppurates :
 Hep., Sil, Graph, Petrol, Sulph. — afl has this symptom.
There is a suppurative tendency viz formation of ulcer.
Suppuration of the lungs after pneumonic haemorrhages
(KaliC), glandular swellings with or without suppuration but
esp, If suppuration be too profuse Cold swellings - abscesses,
slow to suppurate
 Dr. Clarke reports, Merc. intensifies the action of the absor-bents, it may also paralysis them, hence enlargement of glands,
with pricking pains, inflammation, suppuration.
 Dr. Kent reports that marked feature of Merc is the ten-dency to formation of the pus with inflammation, there is
burning and stinging and the rapid formation of pus and the
part is <. by both heat and cold.
3. Rt.-sided affection :
 Dr. Clarke said the hver has been the chief excuse for
Mercurialism in the past and Merc. certainly has a powerful
liver action. The liver ts congested, enlarged, inflarmmed,
stitches in the liver, sens:tiveness in the liver and /nab/lity to
fie on right side. This “< lying on right side “should always
be considered.
4. Chilly «.
 Dr. Nash discussed and amplified that the chill of
Merc. is peculiar. It is nota shaking chill, but is simply a
*‘creeping chilliness’’. (—Gels. big chills with heavy limbs ;
—chills from every movement, from leaving the fire, Nux Vom.).
*-Often when this creeping chilliness ts felt, it is the first symp~
tom of a cold that has been taken and if left alone, the coryza,
sore throat, bronchitis or even pneumonia may follow; but if
taken early, a dose of Merc. may prevent all such troubles.”
The chilliness is fe/t most generally in the evening and
finereases to the night, € not removed by Merc.
 It 1s often felt in single parts. Then again it is felt in
abscesses, and is the harbinger of pus formation.
5. Salivated tongue with thirst :
 There is the characteristic flabby, coated, teeth-indented
 104 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

tongue with foul breath and intense thirst - throat dry and
forepart of the tongue ts moist (Ref : Clarke).
 Ptyalism *: tenacious, soapy, stringy, profuse, foetid, co-ppery, metallic-tasting saliva.
 Tongue : large, flabby, shows imprint of teeth (Chel, Pod.,
Rhus.), painful, with ulcers ; red or white (Ref: Allen’s Key-notes)
Note 1.: Aarely give Merc. if the tongue is dry. (Ref : Gue-rnsey’s Key-notes).
Wote 2. :—Dry tongue but no thirst, Puls., NuxVom., ; —
dry tongue much thirst, Bry, Ars).
6. Offensive discharges, offensive sweat :
 Dr. Clarke said the Mercurius patient is offensive; breath
excessively foetid (Bapt., Carbo. Acid., Kali.P., Nit-Acid , Sil-)
 Sweat : Offensive, mawkish, sweetish.
 Profuse sweat accompaning nearly all complaints and
sweat does not relieve ; tt may even aggravate, <at night
{Ref : Clarke).
7. Leading tremor :
 Dr. Clarke said keynote of Merc. fs tremor. This symptom
is SO pronounced and universal that it renders Merc. the best
general remedy in paralysis agitans. There is tremor of head,
of hands, of tongue. Tremor commencing in the fingers.
 It is the tremor of weakness and paralysis and as described
by B. Cooper it may attack the heart and cause sudden death
on the smallest effort. Short of this there is great tendency
to fainting ; extreme exhaustion after a stool. The tremor
may become jerkings and even convulsions, extreme rest-lessness.
 Dr. Kent said that tremor of the hands, so that the patient
can’t lift anything or eat or write
 Note 1 : Merc. is a grcat remedy in children with epileptiform
fits, twitching and disorderly motions.
Note 2 : The motions of the tongue are disorderly and the
child can't talk. Involuntary motion which can be momenta-rily controlled by volition.
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 105

NATRUN MURIATICUM
 As Dr. John Henry Clarke said, ““Those who can see nothing
but ‘common-salt’ in Natrum Mur. may conclude that they
have not ‘the root of the matter’ in them’ thus allow me to
impress you Natrum Mur. totality through its common name,
i.e ‘Common Salt’’.
 C=-=Consolation aggravates.
 O=On coughing urinates.
 M-= Mapped tongue.
 M = Modialities.
 O—On touch hair falls.
 N=Nervous economy (Ref. Kent)-

 $—Salt craving.
 A=Aversion & abuse.
 L=Losing flesh while living well.
 T=Tremendous emotional and sentimental.
41. Consolation < :
 Dr. Kent said that consolation aggravated the state of
mind—the mefancholy, the fearfulness, sometimes brings on
anger. She appears to bid for sympathy and is mad when
itis given. The patient prefers to be alone ( Ref : Clarke ).
“Wants to be alone to cry.”’
 Nat. Mur. patient A/des their tears for fear of pity and
consolation. ( Ref : Blunt.).
2. On coughing urinates :
 Involuntary urination when walking, coughing, laughing
( Caust., Puls., Sqifla., Arg.N., Zinc.M., Ferr.P.).
3. Mapped tongue :
 Dr Clarke discussed the characteristic tongue of Nat.M.
is either a mapped tongue with red islands, or a clean shining
tongue with froth along each side There are many charac-teristic symptoms in connection with the tongue ;—hair
sensation : numbness and _ stiffness of one side: heavy,
embarassing speech.
 Nat.M. corresponds to children who are late in talking.
 106 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

The tongue is blistered; sticks to roof of mouth. Dryness
of mouth and throat with unquenchable thirst.
 Text says tongue like ringworm on sides (Ars, Lach,
Nit.Ac., Tarax. ).
4 Modalities
 <. from sunrise to sunset esp, 10 0r11 AM
 < at the seashore or from sea air
 > in the open air.
 > while perspiring (Psor.—Rev. of Merc Sol., Ver Alb.).
 > going without regular meals.
 > by lying on right side (—on painful side, Ammon. Carb.,
 Bry., Ign., Puls , Calc.C ).
5. On touch hair falls :
 The hair falls out when touched, in nursing women (Sep.)
Note. : Face oily, shiny, as if greased ( Plb., Thuja. ).
6. Nervous economy :
 The whole nervous economy is in a state of fret and
irritation ( Master Kent. ).
 Great irritability is the characteristic of Nat.Mur patient;
child cross when spoken to.
 Crying from slightest cause, gets Into a passion about
trifles, especially when consoled with
 Hysterical condition of the mind. The lachrymal disposi-tion and hypochondriaca! mood are the key-note of Nat M.
 Marked disposition to weep, sad weeping mood without
cause (Puls ).
 Dreams of robbers in the house, is another pecularity of the
mental condition of Nat.M.
 Tears stream down the face whenever he caughs (Euph.).
7. Salt craving :
 Craving for salt (Cal., Caust., Phos.).
Note : Patient also desires: bitter things, beer, farinaceous
foods, sour things, salt, oysters, fish, milk.
8. Aversion and abuse :
 Aversion to bread, meat, coffee, tobacco. Master Kent
in his Repertory classed Nat.Mur. in first grade under the
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 107

sub-rubric, aversion to bread, China.1, Nat.Mur.?, Con %,
Lyco.*, Nat. S.*, Nit. Ac *, Nux Vom.?, Phos.?, Puls 2,
Sep.*; —aversion to meat, Calc.:, China.*, Graph ?, Mur.Ac.?,
NuxVom.?, Puls 7, Sif +, Sep +, Alumina.*, Carbo.V.2, Lyco.?,
Nat. M.4, Phos.*, Rhus Tox.?.
 Ailments from : Bad effects of anger, abuse of excessive
use of salt, loss of vital fluid (Carbo.Veg., Staph., China.,)
sexual excess, profuse menses.
9. Losing flesh while living well :
 Great emaciation, losing flesh while lving well (Abrot.,
lod, AceticAc , Sanicula , Tuber ,—Ref. Nash); throat and neck
of children emaciate rapidly during summer complaints
(San.c.).
10. Tremendous emotional and sentimental :
 The mentality of Lyco. indicate it’s intellectual side, that of
Nat. Mur. on the emotional and sentimental side.
 Kent said Nat. M.is the chronic of Ign. and where the
later is too superficial, Nat. Mur. cures.
 “Falls in love with the wrong person, and breaks her
heart. Is absurdly obsessed by a foolish passion for a married
man—falls in love with the coachman, and Nat.M., brings
order and sanity.””
NITRIC ACID
 1 wil impress you the totality of Nitric Acid through the
name of the medicine. Know Nitric Acid through Nitric Acid.
 N= Nervous trembling.
 I==Indigestible things craving.
 T=Tremendaus offensiveness ( Ref. Kent ).
 R==Red bloody haemorrhage.
 I= trrestible desire to curse and swear.
 C= Cracks and fissures

 A—Adament but unmoved by apology.
 C=Comes and goes suddenly— pains.
 lin affected part— splinter.
 D-=Debility.
 108 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

1. Nervous trembling :
 Our Nitric Acid pt has nervous trembling After continued
loss of sleep, long lasting anxiety, over-exertion of mind and
body from nursing the sick the pt trembles. Dr N.M
Chowdhury said, fe trembles in all his limbs Master Kent
also reported of this nervous trembling due to prolonged
suffering in broken-down constitution
2. Indigestible things :
 Nitric Acid has craving for indigestible things, such as chalk,
charcoal, stone-chips etc. ( Alumina.*, Calc *, Calc.Phos.?,
others, Cina, Cicutta. Psor. ).
Note. : Great thirstlessness ( Ref : Kent ).
3. Tremendous offensiveness :
 Master Kent said, offensiveness is a marked condition of
the patient, often putrid odors. Offensive leucorrhoea, catarrh,
breath, foetid foot-sweat, strong odors from the body, offen-sive urine Hke that of a horse, —in such cases Nitric Acid
find its, similimum, if the other symptoms agrees.
 Dr. Clarke said, offensive, thin. excoriating discharges — is
the characteristic.
4. Red bloody haemorrhage -
 It is one of our leading haemorrhagic remedy ( Arn.?,
Bell.?, Calc.t, Carbo Veg *, China *, Crot. Hor.?, Ham.?, fpec.?,
Lach.?, Melli?, Merc*, Nat. Mur?, Nit. Ac*, NuxVom.?,
Phos.?. Puls.', Sabina.?, Sep.?, Sulph+*, Acon?, Bov.?,
Elaps.*, Kali Phos.?, Trill?) ( —blood does not coagulate,
Lach.?, Nit. Ac.*, Phos ‘+, } Haemorrhage from bowels tn ty-phoid or typhus ( Crot., Mur.Ac ), after miscarriage, from
over-exertion of body ; bright or dark, profuse haemorrhage.
5. trrestible desire to curse and swear :
 It 1s our Nitric Acid where /rritab/lity is a marked feature.
Pt has irrestible desire to curse and swear. Master Kent placed
it in first grade. (cursing, Anac.*, Nit.Ac.7, Ars.*, Hyos.?,
Lyco *, Nux Vom.?, V.A.? ).
6. Cracks and fissures :
 Dr Clarke said, the localities in which the action of Nit.Ac.
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 109

is very strongly marked,—the muco-cutaneous orifices and
adjoining parts. Cracks and fissures in these selected parts
with splinter like pain, calls for Nit. Ac.. Master Kent said,
fissures forms in many places, canthi, corners of the mouth,
above the anus ; the skin cracks and all these have the splinter
sensation.
7, Adament but unmoved by apolozy :
 This is peculiar uncommon symptom that apolozy is in-capable of moving our Nitric. Acid. Dr. N. M. Chowdhury
said, head-strong, obstinate, but apology, coaxing, love are
equally incapable of moving him.
8. Comes and goes suddenly—pains :
 The pains of Nitric Acid are very characteristic.
Pains : i) Cause : On change of temparature or weather.
 ii) Onset : Comes suddenly, disappears suddenly
 (Bell., Mag Phos }).
 iii) Character : Sticking, pricking as from splinters
( Master Kent in his Repertory classed pain : sensation of
splinters, Agar.*, Arg Nit.*, Hep.', Nit. Ac.? ). Pains gnowing
here and there as from ulcer forming.
Note : Master Kent said, even these pains are aggravated
from noise, ar.
9. in affected part splinter :
 Sensation of splinter in affected parts, ulcers, pifes, throat ;
sensation of a band around head, around the bones (Carb.Ac.,
Sulph. ).
 Dr. Kent remarked, sticking in throat like splinter and can
be bracketed with (Hepar, Natrum.Mur., Alum., Arg- Nit.,
Dolichos ). Master Kent said, sensation as though a_ splinter
felt in inflammed parts, in ulcers and in nerves.
10. Debility :
 As in any other acids ; debility and general weakness (Ref :
Kent) is another denoting feature of deep acting Nitric
Acid. Our sagacious Kent has reported, great general weak-ness, feeble reaction — pt- greatly broken-down by long
sufferings, finally anaemia and emaciation are marked — Nitric
Acid rescues such cases.
 110 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica

NUX VOMICA
 Let me impress you the totality of Nux Vomica through the
common-name, Le. ‘Poison Nut’.
 P=Paralytic conditions (Ref. Kent)
 O=Oversensitiveness (mental and physical).
 l=Ineffectual desire for stool and urine—the general
 cancomitant
 S=Sleep.
 O= Oversensitive to cold.
 N=Nash’s sum-up.

 N=—=Nervous temperament (Ref. Nash)
 U--Universa! antidote.
 T=Trembling.
1. Paralytic conditions :
 Master Kent said, NuxVom. is full of paralytic conditions
The bowels are ina state of excitement but this passes away
and the time comes when the faeces remains in the rectum
with no warning, this extends to the bladder, so that it be-comes full of urine which can’t be voided, or dribbling of
urine; paralysis of the extremities, of the face, of single
muscles : with characteristic sticking pains Nux cures such
cases, provided totality corroborates.

2. Oversensitiveness :
 i) Mentally : Pt. is oversensitrve mentally (Ref : Kent).
irritable, touchy. sensitive cenditions, the woman has impulses
to destory her husband. to throw her child into the fires,
cannot be contradicted—such an aversensitiveness : oversen-sitive to music (Nux Mas.) ; trifling ailments are unbearable,
harmless word offends, such a mental oversensitiveness finds
its similimum in NuxVom.
 ii) Physically . Oversensitive to external impressions, to
light, noise, odors, touch. Pt. ig extremely touchy in regard
to his food and our Master Kent said oversensitive to
Medicines, oversensitive to stimulants. Tendency to faint
from odors, after eating, after every labour pain (Ref. Allen).
  GUIDING SYMPTOMS 111

3 Ineffectual desire for stool and urine—the general
 concomitant .
 ‘Frequent and ineffectual desire to defecate but small
quantities of faeces at each attempt’—this symptom as
Dr. E. B. Nash said, is pure gold There are a few other
remedies that have it, but none so positively and persistently.
It may be coined, that the frequent and in-effectual desire
for stool and urine is a general concomitant symptom.
4. Sieep :
 Sleep is a characteristic indication of Nux Vom. Dr. N. M.
Chowdhury emphasized that the most important point
to remember in this rernedy is that the patients are always
worse after a disturbed sleep. There is_ irrestible desire
to sleep in the evening, can not keep from falling asleep in
the evening while sitting or reading, hours before bed time
and consequently pt. is compelled to retire and sleep. He
wakes up at about 3 A.M. (Ref. Allen) and then falls into a
dreamy sleep early in the morning from which he is hard to
arouse, if aroused, he feels tired and weak. Though Dr.N M
Chowdhury reported, pt. find it difficult to sleep again in the
early morning, ideas keep on crowding upon them till at last
out of sheer exhaustion. he falls asleep again. tried and
irritable (— Puls. point of similarity with Nux Vom., wide awake
in the evening, does not want to go to bed.).
5. Oversensitive to cold :
 Dr. £. B. Nash said, chilliness of Nux Vom. is a character-istic. Great tendency to take cold and aversion or repug-nance to cold air. Pt. is compelled to close the doors and
windows and cover-up the body. Chilly on feast movement,

CHAPTER—4

 PHYSIOLOGICAL ACTIONS
 Phystological action means the action produced by the
drug in its crude form (crude medicinal extract) and in mas-sive dose’ Intrue sense the term or etymology——‘massive
dose’ is apparently vague, as because there are lethal dose,
maximal permissible dose, dosis tolerata or tolerance dose etc.

 Thus as Stedman‘s medica! dictionary explicits the ety-mology—‘physiologic’, which denotes the action of a drug
when given to a healthy person, as distinguished from its
therepeutic action.

 Dr. Stuart Close in his book “‘The genius of Homoeo-pathy—Homoeopathic Philosophy’’—clearly elucidated that,
‘The physiological action of a drug is notits therepeutic or
curative action It is exactly the opposite of a curative action
and is never employed in homoeopathic practice for there-peutic purposes. The use of the word ‘Physiological’ in
conneetion with drug action and drug dosage tends to mis-lead the unwary and just:fy the use of measures which would
otherwise be regarded as illegitimate. In ome word, is ita
euphemism, In as much as the action of the ‘Physiological’
dose and the purpose for which it is given is avowedly to
produce drug syptoms, in a direct and positive manner, that
fact should be clearly expressed in the name, in order that
there may be no misunderstanding.

  CHAPTER-—9
 RELATIONSHIP OF REMEDIES
 ANTIDOTE : Stedman’s Medica! dictionary reveals that anti=against ; dotos=whatis given; ie,
an agent that neutralizes a poison or counteracts its effccts
 Dr. E, A, Farrington elucidated that, there are drugs, which antidote each other Your pt. may be too
susceptible to the action of the remedy, and you require to modify its effects, viz, Farrington explained a
case where he prescribed Nux Vom. for a cold. It has relieved the pt. of his cold, but he became almost
crazy with headache ; ic. due to the fact that he had and excess of Nux Vomica, hence Farrington prescribed
Coffea, and in ten minutes the headache was better This was done by simply modifying the effects of Nux
 RELATIONSHIP

Vomica ; as Coffea counteracted with it ; antidoted the bad effects.
 COMPLEMENTARY : The word comes from complemention ie, which completes. -The term com-plement means that, one drug completes the cure which the other begins ; —but the former drug was unable to
terminate in cure, which the latter does; thus these two drugs are said to be complementary drugs, — viz.,
 OF REMEDIES

Belladonna and Calearea Dr. Clarke said, when a remedy has done all that it can, ima case, then another
remedy is likely to follow up and complete its action, where both are related to the case,—as Bryonia and
Rhus Tox. are complementary drugs.
 Dr. Boenninghausen said, some remedies are in harmony with others, the most similar one, as a rule
are complementary, they antidotes each other's bad effects, follow each other well, and often make-up for the
 Reln.

deficiencies of the others. Others with a lesser degree of similarity may be used at a greater interval of time
and finish up the work started by the other remedies.
 I
  CONCORDANT : The drugs which present marked similarities in action, though dissimilar in origin.
 Drugs holds a concordant relation may follow each other well,— viz , Bryonia and Alumina.
 Reln.
 INIMICAL : There are drugs which have relation of enmity amongst them. They may resembling
 each other apparantly, will not follow one another with any satisfaction ; they seem to mix-up the case (Ref.
 Farrington)— it can also be said that they do harmful effects if followed, or spoils the action of the former,—
 such drugs are said to be inimical between them, —viz., Apis Mel. and Rhus Tox.

Qu. 31. What are the indications of Aconite In fever ?
Ans. a) Node of onset :—
 Acute onset ; sudden and violent like storm.
 b) Causation :—

 iii) From bad effect of checked perspiration
 iv) From fear, fright, shock,
 v) From heat of the sun.
 c) Period of prodrome :—
 High rise of temperature, whole body burning hot.
 d) Period of progress :—
 High fever but of short and sharp attack. Severe
 chill in the evening.
 e) Period of decline :—
 There is no periodicity. recovary is quick.
 f) Physical symptoms :—
 i) Skin— Ory and hot.

 g) Mental symptoms :—
 i) Fear—Great fear of death; predicts the day and
 moment of death.
 ii) Restlessness—Intense nervous restlessness;
 tossing about in agony.
 iii) Anxtety—Anxiety with nervous excitability.
 h) Modalities :—
 Agg. : In evening and towards night; in warm

 Amel. : In open air; by perspiration.

 1) Acon. should never be given simply to control

 no other medicine 1s needed; Acon. will cure

 ii) Rarely indicated in eruptive fever.

 Qu. 10, What is death-rattle ?
 Ans. It's condition where there is accumulation of mucus
 in the resp. tract but patient cannot expectorate it.
 So there is a rattling sound from the chest due to
 violent expiratory effort encountered by the patient,
 as well as from the large amount of the accumulated
 mucus. This sound can be heard from a distance—
 which is known classically as ‘death-rattle’.

 Agg. ) At 12—2 4M. and P.M especially 12~2

 All the complaint are agg. on left side, itis a

 in) Highly seasoned foods.
 iv) Dr. Nash says, whilst Nux Vom. agrees warm
 food best ; but Pulsatilla prefers cold things.
 Kent says, cold foods are digested, while hot
 foods make the body warm, from which symp-toms are worse (Ref. Kent).
 Aversions i) Butter.
 int} Fat and rich foads (Ref Kent).
 fit} Milk.
Qu 24. State the abdominal colic of Pulsatifla.
Ans a) Causation
 i) From taking fatty foods.
 ii) From taking starchy foods.
 iii) From ice-cream, tea, coffee,
 iv) From irregular and protracted menstruation.
 v) From taking pork, cake, etc.
 b) Character of pain
 i) Pains are drawing, tearing, erratic.
 ii) Rapidiy shifts from one part to another.
 iii) Pains are accompanied by constant chilli-ness,
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 251

 iv) More severe the pain, the moresevere the
 chill
 v) Pain appears suddenly, leaves gradually, or
 tension much increases until very acute and
 then “lets up with a snap” ; on first motion.
 c) Modalities
 Agg i) From warmth in general
 i) in the evening, at twilight.
 iii) From taking pork or fat—meats, or from
 fatty foods.
 Amel. By cold food and drinks
 d) Concomitants
 t) Pain with constant chilliness.
 11) Thirstlessness with dry tongue
 tii} Changeability of the symptoms—no two
 symptoms are alike.
 iv} A weak, empty feeling in the stomach, espe-cially in tea-drinkers
Qu. 25. State the diarrhoea of Pulsatilla.
Ans. a} Causation
 i) After taking fatty foods, po:k etc
 ti) After taking frurts
 itt) After taking cold food or drinks, ice-creams
 etc.
 iv) After taking rich foods.
 v) After meals—‘soon as they eat’
 b) Time
 Only or usually at night.

 c) Character of stool
 i) Stool is watery, greenish-—yellowish.
 i) Very changeable, no two stools are alike.
 fii} The stools constantly changes in its colour,
 they are green, yellow, white, watery or
 slimy. This is also foundin cholera infan-tum or entero-colitis of children occurring in
 hot weather. (Ref. Nash)
 252 Palsatilla Nigricans

 iv) Kent says, diarrhoea alternating with cons-tipation with frequent unsuccessful urging
 for stool is a keynote (Ref. Kent).
 v) Kent says, anus remains wide open like Apis
 and Phosphorus
 vi) Dysenteric stool- clear yellow or stools of
 deep green mucus (Ref. Kent).

 d) Modalities
 Agg 1) At might.
 it) After taking fatty foods, ice-creams.
 ui) The diarrhoea and bowel symptoms are agg-ravated in the evening, during night; from
 keeping perfectly still.
 Amel.1) From gentle motion.

 e) Concomitants

 i) Dry tongue with thirstlessness
 ii) Changeability of every symptoms—no two
 symptoms are alike. You never know, what
 you will find the next. (Ref Kent)
 in) Mentally very calm and quiet—mental calm-ness indicates Pulsatilla.
 iv) Or. Nash refers, increased inclination to mic-turate.,

 Qu. 26. Describe the menstruation of Pulsatilla
Ans. a} Introduction
 i) Retarded or delayed menses in young girls
 at the age of puberty. Delayed first mens-truation.
 ii) Patient refers, she 1s never been well since
 puberty.

 b) Causation
 i) From getting the feet wet.
 ii) From cold.
 Note :— Suppression of menstrual flow getting feet wet..
 (Ref. Kent)
 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 253

 c) Time
 Delayed menses, menses comes too late
 Irregular.

 d) Duration
 Too short.

 e) Quantity
 Scanty.

 f) Character of blood
 1) Thick, dark and coagulated. (Ref. Boericke)
 it) Stimy. mixed with clots
 iit) Intermittent flow : flow stops and_= starts
 again.

g) Before menstruation
 i) Weeping mood, sadness and melancholic
 disposition.
 ii) Great nervousness, chilliness.
 iii) Severe abdominal colic with fainting.
 iv} Paleness of the face.
 v) Or. Clarke refers, fits occurring before and
 during menstruation.

h) During menstruation
 i) Sadness, melancholy, weeping mood accom-Panies.
 fi) She can not breathe well in a warm room.
 ii) Violent spasmodic menstrual! colic with pain
 in the abdomen and small of back, causing
 her to bend double (Ref Kent)
 iv) Pain with great restlessness and tossing
 about,—more the pain more the chill. Mas-ter Kent refers, when the menstrual flow is
 present, there is milk in the breast of non-Pregnant women, girls at puberty. (Ref Kent)
 v) Dr. N.M. Chowdhury refers, Pulsatilla is
 prone to menstrual irregularities and parti-cularly at this time her mental phenomena
 254 Palsatilia Nigricans

 undergo strange transformations. She be-comes gloomy and morose. A sort of dread
 pervades her wnole being—the dread of
 eternal damnation. (Ref. N.M. Chowdhury)
 Dr. N. M. Chowdhury refers at night the
 world seems to be on fire and the devil
 dances all around—as the bright fight of hope
 has been extinguished during menstruation.
 vi) Feet red and swollen at the menstrual period,
 ameliorated by the menstrual flow
 1) After menstruation
 i) Milky, thick, white acrid leucorrhoea,
 nu) Contractive pain in the left side of the uterus,
 obliging her to bend double.
 ii) Piles occurring duing and after menses,
 (Ref, Clarke).
 iv) Diarrhoea during and after menses (Ref.
 Boericke).
 j) Modalities
 Agg.i) Flowis more during the day time.
 ii) When she walks about.
 k) Concomitants
 1) Thirstlessness with dry tongue.
 ii) Mild, gentle, timid, yielding disposition.
 iii) = Chilliness: chilly in warm room.
Qu 27. State the laucorrhoea of Pulsatilia.
Ans. a) Subjects
 i} Young girls, especially at the time of
 puberty.
 ii) Never been well since puberty
 b) Character of leucorrhoea
 i) Painless, thick, milky white.
 ii) Acrid, excoriates and corrodes the vulva.
 iii) Leucorrhoea with burning pain.
 iv) Dr. Nash refers feucorrhoeal discharges is
 thick, bland, yellowish and green.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 255

 c) Modalities
 Agg i) Before and during menses
 i) When lying down.
 d) Concomitants
 i) Swelling of the tabia.
 ii) Chilliness, sadness, and peevishness.
 it} Cutting pain in the lower abdomen.
 iv) Gloomy, melancholy, full of tears: lachrymal
 disposition.
 v) Pain in back with tired feeling. (Ref. Boericke)
Ou. 28. State the mental symptoms of Pulsatilla.
Ans 1) Mild
 i) Very gentile,
 ii) Yielding disposition.
 iii) Mid, timid, affectionate,
 iv) Calmness indicates Pulsatilla.
 2) Lachrymal disposition
 i) Inchnation to weep.
 ii) Weeps easily,
 ii) Almost tmpossible to describe her ailments
 without weeping.

 3) Great changeability
 i) Great changeability of all the mental
 symptoms.
 ii) Easily moved from laughter to tears.
 iii) One moment happy, miserable the next.
 4) Aversion
 i) Aversion to opposite sex.
 ii) Aversion to marriage.
 5) Fear
 i) Fear of darkness and ghosts.
 6) Modality
 1) Mental symptoms are ameliorated by con-salation,

chapters.title: Section 25 (Pages 601-625)
chapters.content:
256 Pulsatilla Nigricans

Qu. 29. State the characteristic symptoms of Pulsatilla
Ans. i) Everchanging character of symptoms
 1) Symptoms are ever-changing
 li) No two symptoms are alike, extreme chan-geability. '
 iii} No two stools, no two chills, no two attacks
 are alike
 iv) Very well one hour, very miserable the next,
 apparently contradictory.

 ii) Thirstlessness
 Thirstlessness with nearly all complaints.
 iin) Derangement
 The first serious impairment of health is referred
 to puberic age ‘have never been well since
 puberty’.

 iv) Mind
 i) Very gentle, mild, yielding, weeping dispo-sition
 i) Mental calmness tndicates Pulsatilla.

 v) Pains

 1!) Rapidly shifting pain, shifts from one part
 to another.
 u) Pain with constant chilliness, more the pain
 more the chill.
 ii) Pain appears suddenly, leaves gradually or
 vice-versa
 iv) Pains are drawing, tearing, erratic.
 vi) Discharges
 Secretions from al! the mucous membranes are
 thick, bland and yellowish green, except leu-corrhoea which may be acrid.
 vin) Moenses
 i) Menses irregular too Jate, slimy, scanty,
 protracted, suppressed from getting feet wet.
 ii) Flows mostly during day.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 257

 vill) All gone sensation
 All gone sensation in stomach, specially in tea-drinkers.
 ix) Steep
 i) Wide awake inthe evening ; does not want
 to go to bed.
 i) First sleep restless.
 ui) Sound sleep, when it is time to get up.
 iv) Awakes languid, unfreshed, tired.
 x} Modéalities
 Agg 1) From warmth in general and Amel. from cold
 and from open air.
 ti) Master Kent says, the inflammatory symp-toms, neuralgias and rheumatism are better
 by cold, from eating and drinking cold things
 and cold applications

 RHUS TOXICODENDRON
lu 1 State three medicines for rheumatic diathesis.
Ans 1) Bryonia.
 ui} Colchicum.
 mn} )=©6Rhus Tox,
Qu 2. State a few right sided medicines.
Ans i) Apis Mel,
 ii) BeHadonna.
 iii) Bryonia.
 iv) Causticum.
 vy} Lycopodium.
 vi) Rhus Toxicodendron.
 vii) Podophyilum.
 3. Mention a few medicines where symptoms pro-ceeds from left to right.
Ans. 1) Colchicm
 Pain goes from left to right
 258 Rhus Toxicodendron

 ii) tpecac
 Cutting pain across, the abdomen. from left to
 right.
 iii) Lachesis
 Affections proceeds from left then to the nght.
 iv) Rhus Tox
 Erysipelas : from left to right.

Qu. Describe the pain symptoms of Rhus Tox.

Ans. a) Causation
 i) From spraining or staining a single” part,
 muscle, or tendon.
 ii) From overlifting.
 iii!) Bad effects of getting wet, especially after
 being overheated.

 b) Sensation
 i) Asif sprained.
 ii) «Asif a muscle or tendon was torn from its
 - attachment.
 ii) As if bones were scraped with a knife.
 iv) Lameness, stiffness and pain on first moving
 after rest, or on getting up in the morning.
 v) Affected parts sore to touch,

 c) Character
 i) Cannot remain in bed, must change position
 often to obtain relief from pain.
 ii) Restless. can not stay fong in one position.
 ui) Rheumatic drawing, tearing pains in all the
 limbs, worse at rest and during rough
 stormy weather.
 iv) Back: pain between the shoulders on swa-HNowing ; pain and stiffness'in small of back.
 v) Muscutar cheumatism, sciatica, téft side.
 vi} Rheumatic pain in shoulder joint, Agg. from
 raising the arm laterally. — .
 vii) Aching in left arm with heart disease.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 259

 vit) Tearing pain down the posterior part of limbs,
 during stool.
 d) Modalities
 Agg.i) Pains worse from rest, after midnight,
 ii) in wet rainy weather.
 iti) Backache: Agg. by sitting or lying.
 Amei.i) By walking or continued motion.
 it) Backache amel by iying on something hard.

Qu. 5 State the tongue symptoms of Rhus Tox.

Ans. i) Dry, sore and cracked,
 Wi) Red, with trianguiar rad-tip.
 iti) Takes imprint of teeth.
 iv) Great thirst with dry tongue.

Qu. 6 Mention two medicines for cold sensation in
 larynx on inspiration.
Ans. i) Rhus Tox.
 it} Sulphur.

Qu. 7. State the uvufla symptoms of Rhus Tox.
Ans. 1) Uvuta ; large, dropsical, almost translucent.
 it) Large swelling, but little redness.
Qu. 8. State the eye symptoms of Rhus Tox.
Ans. i) Eyes agglutinated in the morning.
 it) Tears fairly gush out.
 ii!) Swallen, red. oedematous, orbital cellulitis.
 (Ref. Boericke)
 iv) Old injured eyes.
 v) Oedema of lids ; suppurative iritis.
 vi) Intensive ulceration of cornea.
 vii) Eye: painful on turning or pressing it; can hardly
 move it.

Qu 9. State the febrile symptoms of Rhus Tox.
Ans 1. Ailments from
 1) From summer bathing.
 ii) Rainy weather,
 260 Rhus Toxicodendron

 iii) Damp weather especially from cold air,
 walking in damp place.
 iv) Tank or river bathing.
 v) From wetting; getting wet when heated,
 from wetting the head
 vi) Drinking ice-water (Ref. Clarke)
 vil) Over-exertion: etc.
 2. Mode of onset
 Usually there is insidious onset, or when acute
 diseases assume a typhoid form

 3. Symptoms at onset
 i) Rhus Tox may be indicated in any and every
 kind of fevers viz., intermittent, remittent
 and continuous type of fevers.
 ii) In case of intermittent fever there is dry
 teasing cough with taste of blood, followed
 by chill with great thirst and dryness of ton-gue, mouth and throat.
 iii} In case of remittent and conutinuous fever:
 at the onset there ts diarrnoea witn beginning
 of typhoid.
 iv} There is shivering and coldness, generally in
 the evening and accompanied by paroxysms
 of pain and other accessory symptoms
 v) Internal shivering with external heat and
 vice-versa.
 vi) Fever inthe evening; first shivering, then
 heat and thirst (and perspiration); accom-panied and followed by cutting pain and
 diarrhoea.

 4) Symptoms during fever
 i) Shivering and coldness generally in the even-ing and accompanied by paroxysms of
 pain, and other accessory symptoms.
 External coldness atong the skin but does
 —_
 =
 =

 not bear cold air.
 Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 261

 ni) Internal shivering with external heat and
 vice-versa, as if blood is flowing in the veins.
 iv) Fever in the evening, first shivering then
 heat and thirst (and perspiration) accom-panied or followed by cutting pain and
 diarrhoea.
 First headache (throbbing in temples) after-wards chilliness with thirst and tearing
 pains in the limbs,—-afterwards general
 warmth.
 vi) Tertian fever with nette rash, which dis-appears after the attack.
 vii) Double tertian fever: first shivering with
 thirst accompanied by pain in limbs, headache,
 vertigo, pulsative toothache, accumulation
 of saliva in mouth, then general heat with
 shivering on Jeast motion, lastly perspiration.
 During or after the fever: jerks, tingling in
 ears, dry coryza, with restless tossing
 accompanied with nettle rash, pressure at
 the pit of the stomach.
 1x) Patient 1s exceedingly restless in physical
 sphere (+--+-+-++), often changes position in
 bed to obtain relief

 x) Sensitiveness to open air (7~-+-++)

5. Sweat
 1) Fever in the evening., first shivering and
 then heat and thirst with perspiration;
 accompanied or followed by diarrhoea.
 Wt) Headache (throbbing in temples) then
 chilliness with thirst, tearing pain from the
 lumbs afterwards, with general warmth and
 shght chills and finally profuse sour smelling
 perspiration.
 in) Transient heat with perspiration; sweat dur-ing the pains
 262 Rhus Toxicodendron

 iv) Offensive perspiration when seated often
 with violent trembling.
 v)} Nocturnal sweat sometimes with miliary or
 itching eruptions.
 Pulse
 i) Pulse is irregular generally accelerated, but
 weak, soft sometimes it can not be felt or
 is intermittent,
 ii) Pulse : quick and small; coma somnolentum
 with snoring and moans.

 Facial look
 i) Coldness and paleness of the face, alternates
 with heat and redness.
 li) Livid face
 iti) Patient is very much restless and mental
 anxiety Is remarkably present there, and
 both of them are predominently mantfested
 in the facial appearance of Rhus Tox patient.
 Modality
 Agg cold, wet rainy weather, at night, during
 rest (pain aggravates). Amel. in warm dry
 weather, wrapping up, moving affected parts

Qu. 10. Describs the indications of Rhus Tox in Typhoid
 fever.
Ans. Causation
 i) Lying on damp ground, damp cellars, in
 basements,
 ii) From too much summer bathing.
 isi) From getting wet when heated.
 iv) From cold air.
 v} From spraining or straining a single part,
 muscle of tendon, inordinate exertions of
 muscfes; sematic exertion.
 vi) From cold (but not to the grade of Acon.,
 Bell., Bry., Dutc.) (Ref. Clarke)
 Synoptic “lemorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 263

 vil) sin rainy weather.
 viii) From drinking ice-waiter.
 ix) From lying in damp sheets
 x) From wetting head (Ref. Clarke}.
 2. Clinical
 itis suitable in any and every kind of fever,
 intermittent, continous or remittent viz., enteric,
 influenza, dengue, etc.
 3. Mode of onset
 i) Generally, in case of remittent and conti-nuous fever there is insidious onset or when
 acute disease assume a typhoid form,
 ii) Stow pace (Ref. Kent).
 Hi} Onset is marked by diarrhoea, Janguage of
 the text narrates, diarrhoea with begining of
 typhoid.
 4 During remittent fever: general sympto-matology
 1) Restless
 1) Nash’s trio of restless medicine. Must
 change position frequently to obtain
 relief, until the patient is exhausted
 (Ref. Nash).
 i) Kent says, patient never perfectfuily at
 ease and never finds rest.
 iii) Nash says with Rhus Tox restlessness,
 is due to pain and soreness which is
 Amel. by a temporary motion. There is
 a nervous internal uneasiness, which
 makes the patient bound to be on
 motion (Ref. Nash).
 iv) Restless as mation ameleiorates.
 lt} Great rigidity, stiffness, lameness, bruised
 feeling and pain are experienced on first
 movement and Amel. -y walking or conti-nued motion.
 264 Rhus Toxicodendron

 Hl) Great sensitiveness to open air: putting the
 hand out of covering brings on cough
 (Hepar, Rumex.). Needs covering because
 of sensitiveness to open air
 1V) 3) Shivering and coldness, generally in the
 evening, accompanied by paroxysms of
 pain and other accessory symptoms.
 ii) Internal shivering with external heat
 and vice versa.
 uf) Fever in the evening, first shivering
 then heat and thirst.
 Tongue
 i) Triangular red tip tongue (+++) with
 imprint of teeth.
 n) Tongue dry (Ref Nash).
 ni) Cracked, sore with pain
 tv) Dr. Farrington says tongue is dark brown.
 Delirium
 1) Low muttering type of delirium.
 n) Talks about daily occupation
 iii) Patient constantly wants to jump out from
 the bed and tries to escape, tells the thing
 in delirium. (Ref. N.M Chowdhury)
 Dr. N.M Chowdhury says about progres-sive delirium ends’ in stupor when we
 notice a condition similar to Baptisia, Arnica
 ' etc.
 Fever blister
 Fever blister appears around the mouth of the
 chin, corners of the mouth ulcerated.
 Concomitants of remittant fever
 i) Nash says about variola along with typhoid
 symptams.
 it) Diarrhaea with offensive stool.
 int} A bloody, slimy diarrhoea or an involuntary
 stool of cadaverous odour in enteric fever
 (Bapt,, Lach). (Ref, Dr, Dewey)
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 265

 iv) Dryness of mouth with desire for cold drinks.
 (Ref Kent)
 v) Salivation during sieep
 3. Mental generals
 i) Apathy, indifference; refuses the medicine.
 as the patient apprehends those are poison
 ii) Fear of suspicion or being poisoned.
 ii) Kent says,wants to drown himself, yet has
 fear of death
 10. After fever
 i) Paresis or paralytic condition of single
 muscle or of lower limb or ptasis.
 ii) Coryza
 nui) Sleeplessness are aiso marked.
 11. Modality
 Agg. [In midnight. damp wet rainy weathe:
 Agg from rest.
 Agg. at mght (Ref. Kent), from cold in general.
 Amel by continued motion, from warmth ir
 general,
Qu. 11. State the headache symptoms of Rhus Tox.
Ans. a) Causation
 i) From wetting tn rain.
 iit} From river bathing, too much summer
 bathing.
 1) From beer.
 iv) Headache returns from least chagrin.
 b) Location
 i) Especiatly frontal headache.
 ut) Radiating pain from vertex to nose or
 occiput.
 c) Sensation
 i) Brain feels toose when stepping or shaking
 the head,
 ii) Sensation of swashing in the brain.
 iti} As if brain is torn to pieces, stupefying
 headache
 266 Rhus Toxicodendron

 d) Modalities
 Agg. i) By sitting.
 ii) In coid, wet weather.
 iii) During rest.
 Amel. i) From moving the head.
 ii) From warmth,
 6} Concomitants
 i) Red triangular tip tongue.
 ii) Vertigo: when standing or walking, worse
 when lying down, Agg. rising from lying or
 stooping.

Qu. 12. Describe the paralysis of Rhus Tox.
Ans. Introduction
 i) It is one of the Dr. Farrington’s trio of paralysis
 from cold, others are Causticum and Sulphur.
 ii} Rhus Tox especially affects the fibrous tissue,
 tendon, fasciae, sheaths of nerves, ligament and
 tissue, external to joints.
 fii) {itis one of the Dr. E.B. Nash's tria of chronic
 rheumatism and paralysis also.
 a} Causation
 i} From getting wet.
 fi) Lying on damp ground.
 iii) After exertion.
 iv) After parturition.
 v) After typhoid or ague.
 vi) From sexual excess.
Notes .—Rhus Tox has cured many forms of paralysis. Rheumatic
 paraplegia fram getting wet, lying on damp ground
 sleeping in damp sheets, after exertion etc,
 b) Side
 Mainly right sided paralysis. Affects right side
 more, than to the left,
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 267

 c) Type
 Generally acute form of paralysis.
 d} Character of symptoms
 i) Numbness of affected parts.
 ii) Paresis of the limbs.
 tii) Ptosis, drooping of the eyelids.
 iv) Pain: dry, hot, crampy with sore feeling.
 (Ref. Dr. C.M. Boger).
 v) Rheumatic paralysis (Causticum).
 vi) Facial neuralgia, Lumbago, Sciatica (especi-ally of the feft side) with physical
 restlessness.
 vii) Limbs stiff, paralysed (Ref. Boericke)
 viti) Pain along the sciatic nerve.
 ix) Numbness and formication, after over-work and exposure. (Ref. Boericke)
 x} Paralysis : trembling after exertion.
 xi) Loss of power in forearms and _ fingers,
 crawling sensation in the tip of the fingers.
 Tingling in feet. (Ref. Boericke)

 e) Concomitants
 i) Great restlessness.
 it) Red triangutar tip tongue.
 f) Modalities
 Agg. i) In cold, damp weather.
 ii) In rest.
 Amel. From constant motion.
Qu. 13. State the skin symptoms of Rhus Tox ?
Ans. 1) Introduction
 It is an important remedy used for al} types of
 skin diseases, viz., eczema, vesicles, urticaria,
 prurigo, ringworm, erysipelas, cellulitis, herpes,
 Pimples etc.
 268 Rhus Toxicodendron

 2) Eczema
 i) Burning, eczematous eruption with tendency
 to scale formation. (Ref. Boericke)
 i) Surface raw, excoriated, thick crusts.
 i) Eczema in genitals, alternates with dysen-tery. Kent says, cutaneous’ eruptions
 alternates with dysentery or asthma.
 iv) Develops acute eczema over whole body.
 3) Vesicies
 i) Numerous vesicles on skin with red areola
 around.
 i1) Vesicles are swollen and oedematous, tends
 to suppurate (Ref Boericke).
 4) Erysipelas
 i) Yellow vesicles.
 ii) Swelting, burning, itching and stinging pain.
 it) ~=Erysipelas : prcceeds from !eft to rght.
 iv) External genitals: inflamed, erysipelatous,
 oedematous.

 §) Ulcers
 Corners of mouth ulcerated.

 6) Fever blisters
 Around the mouth and on chin.
 7) External genitals
 Inflamed, erysipelatous eruptions, oedematous.

 8) Eruption
 1) Herpetic, pastulous eruption with incessant
 itching, burning and tingling.
 ii) Eruption alternates with dysenteric stools
 and chest pain,

 9) itch
 i) Itching over whole body, especialy on
 hairy parts.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol.2) 269

 u) Eruptions : red, swollen, intense itching.
 iii} Intense itching of genitals, of both sexes.
 iv) Intense itching of reet and ankles.Agg. from
 scratching and warmth of bed.
 10) Cellulitis
 Dr. Dewey in his therapeutics refers, cellulitis
 and corbuncles, with formation of pus, intense
 pain, dark red swelling with prostration.
 11) Urticaria
 i) From getting wet, in cold weather; in every
 spring. (Ref. Kent)
 ii} When Rhus Tox seems indicated but fails to
 cure the chronic urticaria, Bovista to be
 thought of.
 12) Modalities
 AH sorts of skin troubles are Agg from wet rainy
 weather. Amel. from warmth in general and at
 night.
Note :—Dr. Guernsey refers rubing of the affected part agg-ravates the eruption.
Qu. 14. State the characteristic symptoms of Rhus
 Toxicodendron.
Ans. i) Restlessness
 i) Great physical restlessness.
 ii) Dr. Nash’s trio of restless medicine.
 iii) Kent says, Rhus Tox patient is never perfect-fully at ease and never finds rest.
 iil) Modalities
 Agg. during rest, cold, wet, rainy weather,
 from first motion.
 Amel. From continued motion, change of
 position.
Note :—The great characteristic of Rhus Tox is that with few
 exceptions the pains are aggravated during repose and
 ameliorated by motion. (Ref. Allen)
  Rhus Toxicodendron

 iii) Sensation
 Sensation of great rigidity, stiffness, lameness,
 bruished feeling and aching pain in the
 affected parts : Agg. on first movement and
 Amel. by continued motion.

iv) Sensitiveness
 i) Great sensitiveness to open air.
 ii) Putting the hand out of cover brings on
 cough.

v) Desire
 i) Desire for cold milk which ameliorates the
 gastric complaints.
 ii) Desire for sweet, beer etc.

vi) Adoptability

 i) Adapted to persons of rheumatic diathesis.
 ii) Bad effects of getting wet, especially after
 being overheated.

 Ailments from
 i) From spraining or straining a single part,
 muscle or tendon,
 li) Overlifting, particularly from stretching high
 up to reach things.
 ii} =Lying on damp ground.
 iv} Foo much summer bathing, river bathing etc.

 Right sided medicine
 i} Itis predominantly a right sided medicine.
 fi) Affects right more than the left.

ix} Dreams
 i) Oreams of great exertion.
 ji) Oreams of rowing. swimming, working hard,
 dreams of his daily occupation etc.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) 271

 SECALE CORNUTUM
Qu. 1. Mention three medicines suitable for anaemic
 women.
Ans. #1) Natrum Mur.
 ii) Pulsatiila.
 iii) Secale Cor.

Qu, 2. State the haemorrhage of Secale Cor.
Ans I. Adoptability
 1) Women of thin, scrawny, feeble, cachectic
 appearance ; irritable nervous temperament.
 ii) Pale, sunken countenance.
 tii) Viomen of very fax muscular fibre, every-thing seems loose and open: no action;
 vessels flabby.

 il. Character
 i} Haemorrhagic diathesis : copiaus flow of
 thin, black, watery blood: the corpuscles are
 destroyed,
 ii) The slightest wound causes bieeding for
 weeks.
 iii} Discharge of sanious liquid blood with a
 strong tendency to putrescence,
 iv) Tingling in the limbs and great debility ;
 especially when the weakness is not caused
 by previous foss of fluids.

 5. Head sweats profusely during sleep : Ca/c. carb.
 6. Sweaton the face on a smali spot only while eating :
 lgnatia.
 7. Alternate sweat with dryness of the skin : Apfs.
 8. Free sweat: &ryonia.
 9. Night sweats : China., Merc. so!., Sil.

Oral 62 Qral Materia Medica

10. Morning sweat setting in after waking : Su/ph.
41. Orenching sweat : Aconite, Belladonna, Mercurius.
12. Free sweat but the pains keep the patient still: Sry.
43. Sweat has the odour of sulphur : Phosphorus.
14. Genital sweat has the odour of honey: Thuja.
15. Offensive sweat : Baptisia., Merc., Silicea.
16. Offensive sweat of the feet: Sar. carb.. Graph., Kalf
 carb., Nit. ac., Sil.
17. Offensive foot sweat; toes and soles get sore: BSaryta
 carb.
18. Weakening night sweats untill morning : China.
19. Sweat only while sleeping, stops when awaking : China,
 Thuja.
20. Sweat with chilliness on least uncovering : Nux vom.
21. Sour sweat: Cale., Hepar sulph., Thuja.
22. One sided sweat: Puls., Lyco.
 23. Profuse sweat day and night without relief : Hepar sulph.
 24, Sweat only in the uncovered’ parts or all over except
 head: Thuja.
 26. Sweat in the covered parts : Bel/., Cham.
 26. Sweat all over except head : Thuja (Rev. of Sil.).
 27. Sweat particularly in the parts rested upon : Acon.
 28, Head sweets profusely while sleeping, wetting the
 pillow far around : Ca/c., Si/.
 Sweat only on head or on head and face : Sif.
 30. Sweat over the entire body during walking’: Ca/c. carb.,
 Nux vom.
 31. Sweat during fever without relief, rather aggravates:
 Merc. sol.
 32. Sweat aggravates all complaints : Merc., Verat. afb.
 33 Sweat ameliorates all complaints : Nat. mur.
 34. Old broken down cases of malaria ; chill ; greasy sweat :
 Lyeoa,
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) Oral 63

35. Sweat relieves the fever : China.
36. Sweat relieves the pain during fever : Acon.

TEMPERAMENT :
 1. Sanguine temp.: Acon., Arn... Hyos., Phos, Silicea,
 Ver alb.
 2. Nervous temp. : Acon., Apis., Arn., Cham., Gels., lgn..
 Nit ac., Phos., Sec. cor., Suiph.
 3. Phlegmatic: Puls.
 4. Bilious : Be//., Nux vom., Podo.
 6. Melancholic: Caust, Lach., Nux vom.
 6. Hysterical: Gels., /gn., Nat. mur.
 7. Lymphatic: Bapt , Bell.
 8. Irritable : Ap/s., Arg. met., Ars.. Bell , Cina., Colo , Lyce,
 Nat. mur., Nux vom., Secale., Sil.

THIRST :
 1. Thirst for large quantity of cold water: Acon.
 2. Thirst for small quantity of very cold water: Hyos
 Phos., Veratrum.
 3. Intense thirst with moist tongue : Merc.
 4. Thirst for coldest drinks ; wants ice : Phos., Veratrum.
 5. Thirst in chill stage of fever : Ap/s , ignatia.
 6. Thirst for large quantities of cold water: Acon., Bry
 Mercurius. Pode., Ver. alb.
 7. Orinks much eats little: Su/ph.
 8. No thirst during chill: Gels.
 8. Unquenchible thirst for small quantity Of water at short
 interval (often but little at a time) : Avs. a/b.
10. No thirst with dry tongue : Pufls.
 11. Thirst for acid or sour water : Sec. cor., Verat. afb.
12. Complete thirstlessness : Aethusa., Apis., Gels,
 Ipecac., Puls.
 Oral 64 Oral Materia Medica

 13. Thirsty : Acon., Ars., Bry., Cale., Phos, Nat. mur.,
 Veratrum.
 44. Thirst for ice-cold water but vomited as soon as it gets
 warm in the stomach : Phos.
 15. Absence of thirst with scanty urination : Ap/s.

 THROAT TROUBLES:
 1. Splinter like sensation in the throat: Arg. nit., Hepar.
 2. Pricking pain worse when swallowing : Nit. ac.
 3. Raw spot over the bifurcation of the trachea : Arg. met.
 4. Great sense of rawness and dryness in throat : Caust
 5. Putrid sore throat, tendency to gangrene : Ammon. carb.
 6. Throat complaints begins in left and goes to right side :
 Lach.
 Hoarseness of professional singers, public speakers, etc. :
 Arg met.
 Painless hoarseness agg. in morning : Ca/c.
 Hoarseness agg. in evening : Acon., Carbo veg., Phos.
 Hoarseness in the afternoon with cough : Carbo veg.,
 Phos.
11. Chronic laryngitis of singers : Arg. nit.
12. Loss of voice from over heating : Anf. crud.
13. Frequeut swatlowing, as if to swallow something down
 the throat: Cine.
14. Sensation as if a splinter or fish-bone were sticking in
 the throat: Arg. nit., Flepar., Nit. ac., Sil.
15. Sensation of splinter were lodged in the throat, when
 swallowing, breathing or moving the neek : Arg. nit.
16. Throat iooks very dry, fairly glistening : Phos.
17. Painiess sore throat: Baptisia.
18. Throat affections after suppressed foot sweat: Baryta
 carb.
19. Rawness and soreness in the throat : Caust.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) Oral 65

20. Sore throat feels better when swallowing : /gnatia.
21. Can swallow liquids only : Saptisia., Baryta carb.
22. Liquids are more painful than solids : Laches/s
23. Cannot talk ; larynx is so painful : Phos.
24. Oedematous, bladder like appearance of uvula: Ka/i bich.
25. Can swallow liquids only but has aversion to them:
 Silicea.
26. When patient drinks, quid descends with gurgling
 sound ; Ars., Thuja.
27. Paintess hoarseness agg. in the morning : Ca/e. os.

TIME MODALITIES :
 1. Aggravation at 3 a.m. : Thuja.
2. - at 3 to 4 a.m. : Ammon. carb., Nux.
 3. ” at § a.m.: Cinchona.
 4. ‘ at7 am.: Podo.
 5. ” at 9 a.m. : Cham
 6. o at 10 a.m.: Gels.
7. - at 11 a.m.: Nat. mur, Sulph.
 8. o at 12 a.m.: Ars. a/b., Zincum.
 9. at 12 to 2 a.m. & p.m. : Arsenic.
10. » , at3a.m. & p.m.: Thuja.
11. 1 at 3 p.m.: Apis.
72. 1 at 4to 8p.m.: Lyco., Hell.
13. ” at 6to 9 p.m.: Colc., Mag. phos.
14. at9pm.: Bry.
15. at first night : Puls.
16. oo at last night : Nux.
17. Whole day: Nat. mur., Thuja.
18. Whole night: Aurum met., Merc.
*For details of time modalities : Consult :
 *CLOCK-WISE AGGRAVATION CHART’ of
 S. K. BANERJEA, (Author), Published by Harjeet & Co.,
 New Delhi.
 Ora) 66 Ora) Materia Medica

TONGUE :
 1. A thick, milky white coated tongue : Ant. crud.
 2. Lead cotoured tongue: Ars. a/b.
 3. White coated with reddened papillae and red edges, red
 “in streaks, dry in the middle : Ant. tart.
 4. Dry tongue with thirst for large quantities of cold water
 with bitter taste : Bry.
 5. During talking or chewing they bite themselves in the
 cheek or tongue : /gn.
 6. Mapped tongue with red insular patches—like ring~
 worms on sides: Ars. alb., Lach., Merc. sol., Nat. mur.,
 Nit. ac.
 7. Bad taste in the mouth, esp. early in the morning, or
 nothing tastes good or no taste at all : Pu/s.
 8 Red triangular tipped tongue with imprint of teeth and
 bitter taste : AMferc., Podo., Rhus tox.
 9. Heavy trembling of tongue, with failing of lower jaw (in
 typhoid state) : Lyco.
10. Dry, black tongue, trembles; protruded with difficulty :
 Lach.
11. Great complaints about the dryness of the tongue, which
 is not very dry: Nat mur.
12. Large tongue shows imprint of teeth which is dry, sore
 and cracked : AAus tex,
13. White coating only on one side of the tongue ;
 Rhus tox.
14. White coating on both the sides : Caust.
16. Constant prostration and retraction of tongue like a
 snake: Lach.
16. Cold tongue at the last stage of any disease, with cold
 sweat: Carbo veg.
17. Posterior part coated, anterlor part clean with bitter or
 sour taste : Nux vom.
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) Oral 67

18. Completely dry tongue and parched with thirstlessness :
 Puls.
19. Tongue and jaws becomes lame if cold air or water chilis
 him: Dule.
20. Numbness of the tongue; feels so thick that he can
 hardly speak, partial paralysis : Gels.
21, Speechiessness from paralysis of the organs of speech :
 Caust.
22. Great dryness of mouth and tongue ; lips parched and
 dry: Bry.
23. Mouth is very dry; tongue dry, brown in a streak down
 the centre: Bapt.
24. Protruding of the tongue with a silly expression: Lyco.
25. Tongue smooth, red and cracked : Kaff bich.
26. Tongue painfully sensitive when chewing gums becomss
 loosened and retracted from teeth: Carbo veg.
27. Looseness of teeth, with bleeding gums, which ara
 very sensitive when chewing : Carbo veg.
28. Grinding teeth and rolling head from side to side with
 moaning : Podo.
29. Warts on the back of the tongue: Caust.
30. Tongue oscillating fram side to side Ike a pendulum :
 Lyco.
31. Tongue having thick yollow coating at base: Ka/i hich.

TOOTHACHE & TEETH SYMPTOMS :
 1. Toothache when child takes the breast: China.
 Decayed toothache generally better at night, can't bear
 to be touched by the tongue: Ant. crud.
 Toothache during menses : Ammon. carb.
 Teeth comes en masse ' Caust.
a

 Toothache better by holding cald water: S&ry, Cheir.,
 Caust , Puls.
 Oral 68 Oral Materia Medica

 6. Toothache of wash-women or from washing clothes:
 Phos.
 7. Toothache pulsating tearing, pain shoots into face or
 upto ears: Mercurius.
 8. Grinding of the teeth and tossing during sleep ; always
 cross when awake: Cina

 9. Toothache relieved by holding hot water: Ars., Hepar.
 10. Toothache relieved by taking cold water & cold air: Bry.
441, Looseness of teeth, easily bleeding gums : Carbo veg.
 12. Patient feels toothache alltimes but not during chill:
 fon.
 13. Toothache during pregnancy : Cham.
 14, Teeth decay at root but crown remains sound: Thuja
 (opp. to Staph).
 15. Teeth crumble, turn yellow : Thuja,
 16. On blowing the noses, a pressing pain in the hollow
 tooth or at the side of it: Thuja.
 17. Intense congestion of the brain in childran, during den-tition : Gels.
 18. Toothache not relieved by heat or cold but oniy by
 rubbing the check : Merc. sol.
 13. Excessive bleeding from gums after teeth extraction:
 Phosphorus.
 20. Toothache from tea drinking : Thuja.

 URINARY SYMPTOMS :
 1. Cannot pass urine if, others are present: Heper.,
 Nat. mur.
 Urine strong smelling, like horses’ urine : Nit. acid.
 Involuntary micturition ; constant dribbling; paralysis
 of sphincter vesicae : Be//.

 4. Cold sensation when urine passes : Nit. acid. ~
  Synoptic Memorizer of Materia Medica (Vol. 2) Oral 69

 5. involuntary urination during laughing, coughing, etc. :
 Arg. nit., Causticum, Nat. mur, Puls.

 Every time he passes urine feels as if stool would pass :
 Aloe.
 Scanty urine : Apis., Colchicum., Heileborus.
 Scanty urination with absence of thirst : Ap/s.
 Profuse urine : Merceurius, Nat. mur., Siicea, Sulphur.
 Numbness or insensibility of urethra: can not fell when
 the urine is passing in the dark, only by sense of touch :
 Caust
17. Brick dust sediment in urine : Merc. cor.
12. Urine almost black, foamy, frequent, dark : Lach.
13. Red sand in urine : Lycopodium.
14. Bloody urine from mechanical cause : Arnica.
15. Brown sand-in urine: Nit. ae.
16. Scanty urine, dark sediment like coffee grounds : Apis.

17. Urine passes unconsciously day & night: Arg. niz.,
 Caust., Puls.
18. As if some urine remains after urinating : Gerb. vu/g.
19. As if urine is always trickling in the urethra : TAu/a.
20. Incontinence of urine with great irritation of the parts
 agg. at night, when coughing : Apis
21. Inky urine : Apis., Co/ehicum.

22. Scanty urine in drops with white sediment and with
 presence of blood, albumin, suger: Co/ch.
23. Cutting in the urethra after micturition : Nat. mur.
24. Urine voided slowly drop by drop without ‘force:
 Hepar sulph.
26. Retention of urine with great desire, which is greatly
 worse on lying, esp. on the back : Puls.
26. Retention of urine in new born baby : Acon., Caust.
27. Retention of urine, has no dasire to pass it : Ars.
 Oral 70 Oral Materia Medica

28. Quantity of urine voided ts larger than the amount of
 water drunk: Merc.
23. Milky-white urine : Cina, Duic.
30. Greenish urine: Ars., Berb. vulg.
31. Enuresis in children : Cina, Ca/e. carb.
32. Child cries before urination : Lyco.
33. Enuresis in old people : Seca/e cor.
34. Urine looks like milk mixed with jelly : Ou/e.
35. Large quantity of colourless urine : Su/phur.
36. Urine drops vertically : Hepar.
37. Headache amel. by profuse urination: /gn, Gels.,
 Silicea, Verat. alb.
38. Sensation of ball rolling tn the bladder: Lach
 39. Movement agg. urinary complaints : Berb.
 40. Urina red, black, scanty, coffee ground sediment: He//.
 41. Urine turbid when passed ; turns milky & semi-solid on
 standing : Cina.
 42. Atthe end of urination severe cutting pain in urethra:
 Berb., Nat. mur., Nit. acid., Thuja.
 43. Patient wishss to pass urine on seeing running water:
 Suiph.
 44. Stitches in the neck of the bladder and anus at the same
 time : Lyco.
 45. Pain radiating from renal region ; extending to thighs :
 Berb.

 VERTIGO:
 1. Vertigo on looking down : Phos., Sul/ph.
 2. Vertigo on looking up: Puls., Sificea.
 3. Vertigo when closing the eyes : Arg. nit., Lach., Thuja.
 4. Vertigo on ascending : Ars., Calc. os.
 5. Vertigo when stooping or on every change of position :
 Bell,
